DrugAnalysis.description: Biopharma decision engine tracking publicly traded companies against FDA drug decisions, verified stock-price reactions and clinical-pipeline success rates, rendered as a dependency-free static site with no build step. The project is now at v29 (2026-09-22) and the whole-table census has landed: the official Drugs@FDA Submissions.txt holds 193,810 rows, and the boundary the project defends holds over all of them — 0 rows are dated between the FD&C Act (1938-06-25) and 1938-12-31. That census also contradicted two of the project's own v28 working hypotheses and v29 publishes the contradictions verbatim rather than smoothing them: the before-1939 window holds 1 row rather than 0 (ApplNo 060904, ORIG 1, AP, dated 1900-01-01, a pre-statute placeholder published as FLAG-PRE-STATUTE-DATE with counted_as_fda_decision false), the undated window holds 8 rows (1 ORIG on 009658 plus 7 SUPPL) enumerated as FLAG-UNDATED-ROW, and the arithmetic 193,810 = 1 + 8 + 193,801 is stated in the artifact. The status census over the complete table is AP 192,604 / TA 1,205 / empty 1 — not the AP-only census v28 expected — with TA defined verbatim from FDA's own Drugs@FDA glossary as a tentative approval that does not allow marketing, so the project's wording was refined from 'approval actions only' to 'approval-family actions only (AP, TA)'; the type census is ORIG 27,862 / SUPPL 165,948 and the builder now aborts on any status outside {AP, TA, empty}. ApplNos 060904 and 009658 have no row in the official Applications table in either publication, appear in no committed window and in no project table, and render no application section on their official overview pages — no cause is inferred. Two corrections are recorded as corrections, not as footnotes: v28 wrote that NDA000159 was already counted in data/pre1965_fda_decisions.csv, which was false (that table holds NME-comparable rows only, earliest 1942, and NDA000159 is row PRE1965AUDIT-1939-02 of the pre-1965 originals audit table), and the same error class had already been caught for NDA000004 in v28. GEMSDOE.title: GEMSDOE — Geologic Mapping Prize Challenge
GEMSDOE.description: Evidence-backed working site for the DOE GEMS Prize Challenge on DrivenData — predicting geothermal faults in the GeoDAWN region under a distance-weighted Tversky metric, with a 19-band feature stack, a $300,000 prize pool split $50,000 initial and $250,000 final, ending 2026-12-03 at 11:59 p.m. UTC. STATUS.md at commit cf20e1b records session 23 (2026-09-22), which made it possible to generate a submission from the site itself in the browser with no install and no GPU: scripts/build_submission_payload.py encodes the adopted artifact into docs/submission_field.bin (a gems-rle-v1 uleb128 run-length stream, 532,174 bytes for 259,549 runs) with a manifest of grid, transform, EPSG, resolution, value counts, blob hash, artifact hash and 17 named checks, where --check re-derives the manifest from the raster and refuses if any pin drifted and --verify decodes the blob and compares float32 bits; docs/geotiff_writer.js is a dependency-free TIFF/ZIP writer in plain JS with real deflate, and the CLI and CI routes produce the same bytes. Session 21 closed the standing data-placement blocker in-sandbox: scripts/assemble_data_bridge.py reassembled all three official rasters from committed parts in 2.8 s with every part and whole-file sha256 verified (training_features.tif 418,912,844 B, labels.tif 425,830 B, sample_submission.tif 1,599,597 B), and scripts/prepare_data.py passed on the placed bytes (3292x3730, 19 bands, EPSG:32611, 100 m, aligned bounds, band tags present); scripts/baseline_submission.py then reproduced the committed submission.tif byte for byte (sha256 9f2577cff20d...) in about 17 minutes on 2 vCPU with no torch, and scripts/validate_submission.py passed all 8 checks on the fresh file. The scientific stance remains deliberately unhedged and unclaimed: all four block-holdout folds are committed and the memorisation-versus-transfer gap is reported as a spread rather than a point — fold 0 +0.0114, fold 1 -0.0070, fold 2 +0.0139, fold 3 +0.0093, mean +0.006904, spread 0.020935, positive in 3 of 4 — and because no fold reaches the 12 resampling units a readable block-bootstrap interval needs, the scorer itself flags every per-fold interval interval_readable false, so the honest reading is 'no clear memorisation, no clear transfer gain' with the full-grid 0.099859 (reproduced digit-for-digit on a runner) retained as the selection statistic. The pseudo-label contrast has fired twice and STATUS.md is explicit that quoting either fire alone would overstate the precision: the first gave held-out blocks 0.0806 to 0.1841 (+0.1036, P=0.999) on the new-fault-like proxy against 0.2113 to 0.1239 (-0.0874, P=0.001) on catalogue labels, and the second — same seed, same config, same partition, different runner — measured proxy +0.0677 and catalogue -0.1079, a roughly 0.036 run-to-run swing on the proxy arm of the same order as the +0.0313 union contrast itself; the two scopes also disagree in sign on the union (+0.0313 held-out against -0.0375 trained-on), which STATUS.md calls instability rather than a result. Against the paired block-bootstrap bar its own FIELD rule uses (P >= 0.95) the union contrast reaches P = 0.916 with an interval spanning zero on 8 scoreable blocks, so it is suggestive and not established, both verdicts carry shippable_evidence false, and the circularity is derived rather than asserted because the pseudo-label path is the same proxy_catalogue.tif the proxy truth is cut from. A third population is the disjoint 122,652-pixel union (60,988 + 61,664, disjointness verified at score time). STATUS.md also defuses one coincidence on purpose: the baseline's union held-out DTI of 0.197183 resembles the public leaderboard's top score of 0.1972, and the two are unrelated quantities. IRREGULARITY: the repository's own test suite fails at this head — `python3 -m pytest tests -q` gives 467 passed, 32 skipped and 1 FAILED (tests/test_site_pages.py::test_the_build_reproduces_the_committed_pages), and 32 of the skips are environment-gated rather than the 1 STATUS.md reports (IRR-102). The next-session ordering stands at item 8 (the only unbiased signal: enroll and first upload, against a bar of 0.2854 as of 2026-09-21), then 3, then 6, then firing the pseudo-label workflow for folds 1-3 so the pool crosses 12 units before the runner artifacts expire around 2026-10-03.

MLB-Live-PBP.title: MLB Live PBP — Scoreboard & Play-by-Play
MLB-Live-PBP.description: Zero-dependency static web app that pulls live MLB game data straight from the public MLB StatsAPI and renders it in a Gameday-style scoreboard, re-implemented from scratch in vanilla HTML/CSS/JS with no build step, no frameworks and no API keys. Two views: a scoreboard showing every game for any date with live scores, inning, count, probable pitchers and W/L/S decisions, and a game view showing who is at bat, who is pitching, the count, outs, runners on base, on-deck and in-the-hole hitters, pitch counts, last play, inning-by-inning linescore, full box score and the complete play-by-play timeline with pitch-by-pitch detail. A third surface is devoted to replay: an all-games Replay Feed page pulls review events from every game on the schedule — manager challenges, crew chief reviews, umpire reviews and ABS pitch challenges — with game link, inning, challenging team, reason, outcome, batter/pitcher context and a three-row review score tracker (Before review, Possible after, Actual after) that explicitly refuses to treat the possible score as a prediction, marks Before/Possible as not observed when the page opens only after resolution, and never assigns a later end-of-plate-appearance score to an earlier pitch review. A Runs at Risk mechanism decides from the data rather than the review type whether the call on the field credited runs to the very event under review — a run counts only when the official payload has a runners[] record with details.isScoringEvent true whose details.playIndex matches the reviewed event — and fires once per review with a chime, an optional desktop notification and a persistent banner, never predicting the ruling. Review detection reads the API's own status registry rather than matching the words challenge/review, because that missed crew-chief reviews whose official detailedState is 'Instant Replay'. The challenge counters are the official StatsAPI counters read as-is (review.away/home.used/remaining and gameData.absChallenges.away/home), never counts derived from feed events, never zero-filled when absent, and a used-counter that moves backwards between polls is flagged on the row as an irregularity instead of being silently corrected. A two-sided hit forecast compounds the batter's and pitcher's season rates by log5 with real platoon splits, recent form, head-to-head history, same-game familiarity and the live count into a single probability with a matchup tier and per-driver point adjustments. Auto-refresh runs at 500ms for the full feed with a 250ms status watcher for the whole slate, and a lean play-by-play probe at 250ms while a review is in flight. LIMITATION: the offline test suites run here — 14 of the 15 tools/*-test.mjs suites pass — but tools/smoke-test.mjs reports 8 checks failed in this sandbox because it fetches the live statsapi.mlb.com teams directory, gameStatus registry and review-status projection and this audit environment has no egress to that host, so that result is an environment limit rather than evidence of a repository defect.

MLB-PBP.title: MLB Plaintext Play-by-Play Viewer
MLB-PBP.description: Searchable web viewer and reproducible archive pipeline for MLB regular-season and postseason games from 2014 forward, using exactly one source: HTTPS responses from MLB's own statsapi.mlb.com domain. It does not invent, estimate, silently repair or manually enter a score, name, play or measurement — the raw download is the exact official response body and the human-readable files are deterministic projections of fields in that response. It browses the official schedule by date and includes MLB sportId=1 game types R, F, D, L and W (regular season and postseason) while excluding Spring Training, exhibitions and the All-Star Game, renders line scores, decisions, every play, pitch and action details, runner movements and batting and pitching box scores, searches a game's official descriptions and player names in the browser, and downloads a readable .txt report, the complete raw .json or an event-oriented .ndjson without a server or account. A bulk archive runs from January 1, 2014 through any requested end date with retries, rate limiting, resume support, provenance checks and checksums, live games refresh automatically using the wait interval returned in MLB's feed, and while a game is Live the pipeline logs transient official events — score changes, official-scorer ruling changes, scoring-pending rulings and boundary calls — into a per-game Event log tab stored locally in the browser so it can be reopened after the event or the game is over. A response is accepted only if the URL is HTTPS on the exact statsapi.mlb.com host, the response is successful JSON, it contains MLB Advanced Media's provenance notice, and a game feed's returned gamePk matches the requested gamePk. The site has no sample scores and no fallback dataset: if the official endpoint cannot be reached or does not return a value, the interface says so. The repository does not relicense MLB data — every saved record keeps MLB Advanced Media's returned notice, the exact source URL, the UTC retrieval time and a SHA-256 digest, and users remain responsible for complying with MLB's terms. The site is dependency-free static HTML, CSS and JavaScript in docs/ that requests data directly from MLB in the visitor's browser, with no third-party analytics, proxy, database, generated game content, logo or team artwork. OLBG-Competition.title: Northstar Competition Lab — OLBG Tipster Paper Trading
OLBG-Competition.description: Evidence-first research platform for the betting market: no bookmaker, exchange, tipster, payment-processing or order-placement client anywhere, only a local append-only paper ledger, public league data feeds, offline backtests and a deliberately dormant forward-test desk. docs/FACTS.md (nr-facts-2026-09-22.1) is the canonical generated fact sheet and the repository's own tests/test_facts.py enforces that the site agrees with it; the offline suite was executed here and passes (441 test functions collected from the sources, 499 cases after pytest expands the parametrised ones). FACT sheet numbers at this head: 441 test functions, 153 open anomalies (99 RESULT_KIND_INCONSISTENT, 48 SOURCE_EDITED, 5 TIME_CONFLICT, 1 MISSING_METADATA) and 17 hash-verified fixtures with an aggregate sha256 of 2dfbb756c66a771d2cb4a47797bdb02b8343165ba6911f893dd942cc2e68b9af. Its evidence table records 3 verified sports — football as pilot_verified, darts and ice hockey as results_pilot — and 18 as verification_blocked. The football pilot is a frozen 27-match Bundesliga 1 2024/25 sample (matchdays 1, 10, 20) with 27/27 dual-source agreement against football-data.co.uk, and the engine output has grown to 829 odds snapshots (405 on 1X2, 208 on over/under 2.5 and 216 on Asian handicap) across 13 PnL desks, twelve of the thirteen negative. The one positive desk, ah-poisson-value-v1, shows +9.8 u at a +44.7% ROI, but its Holm-adjusted p is 0.0715 against a family size of 13, so it is not significant and the repository claims no edge; dixon-coles-v1's +5.0 u at p_raw 0.475 is likewise not significant. New this pass: full-season football accuracy desks over 306 results, where elo-favourite-3way-v1 calls 167 times at 52.1% against the 38.6% always-home baseline, and a Poisson totals desk at 61.1% against the always-over baseline's 59.8%. Ice hockey runs on the whole DEL 2024/25 season (428 events) with 7 prediction-only desks and no odds path: plain Elo makes 243 calls at 66.3% (Brier 0.446) against the always-home baseline's 59.8% over 323 calls, margin-of-victory Elo 255 calls at 65.5%, regulation 3-way Poisson 64.7% against regulation-home 59.4%, and totals O/U 5.5 Poisson at 52.3% — below the always-over baseline's 53.6%. Darts runs a 425-event 2025-26 pool (423 finished, 8 events): on the cold 2025 pool of 141 matches darts-elo-v1 made 0 selections because the maximum probability of 0.551 never cleared the 0.60 threshold, while the widened 2025-26 pool produced 48 calls graded 39 of 48 correct at 81.25% with Brier 0.349, beating the listed-first baseline's 66.3% on 421 calls; the new margin-of-victory desk adds 111 calls at 78.4%, Brier 0.358. The forward desk is live on 284 frozen pre-kickoff calls awaiting a result. OpenLigaDB data is used under ODbL 1.0 with attribution; TradingView's December 2025 rules page is cited only as an event-classification example.

ShoulderPain.title: ShoulderPain — Research-Backed Shoulder & Scapula Pain Guide
ShoulderPain.description: Source-linked GitHub Pages guide to shoulder and shoulder-blade ('wing') pain, written around one stated context — a male adult aged about 36-40, left-side sleeping, a possible workout injury, prolonged computer use and limited room space — and explicitly educational information rather than a diagnosis or a personalised rehabilitation plan, with emergency and urgent warning signs given priority over exercises, furniture or symptom logging. Ten pages share one static template and compact navigation: start, medical advice, treatment, exercises, desk and room, furniture and prices, care costs, an optional log, sources and audit, and next steps; all research content works without JavaScript and no sign-in or symptom entry is required. The current revision is a deliberate narrowing rather than an expansion. It reviewed the pre-existing site at commit e1c63c4 and, in its own words, 'replaces blanket verification/completeness claims with a narrower, auditable source register, simplifies the UI and corrects unsafe or unverified assumptions', keeping the previous site in Git history. Twenty official pages were opened directly on 2026-09-20 — MedlinePlus, NHS, AAOS/ASES, CSP, OSHA, CMS, five furniture manufacturers or sellers, and Luna — and data/sources.json records each source's section, a short excerpt, its scope and its check date, with government and medical-society guidance kept separate from commercial product information. data/claims.json maps source-bearing content units to references and source-file lines: 90 review units, described as a review aid and 'not an automated truth certificate'. Exercises were reduced to four source-checked examples carrying exact AAOS HTML doses and supervision boundaries. Five furniture listings give exact variant and price boundaries with folding trade-offs, and no product is claimed to fit an unmeasured room or to treat shoulder pain; the one care price quoted is an official provider example ($135 self-pay per visit at Luna), not a nationwide average, and other unverified medical costs are explicitly left unpriced. REVIEW.md documents three passes and eight source irregularities found while reading, including a COMHOMA price where $54.49 was the selected White variant and $25.50 the discount, a VIVO desk that folds against the wall but is not quickly detached, a Lillipad whose specifications claim a 700 lb static test while its FAQ says 350 lb and neither replaces the 75 lb operational rating, and a Luna search excerpt showing $125 where both directly opened pages showed $135. The optional log is local-only, retains the `shoulderpain-log-v1` key so prior entries can still be read or imported if valid, and validates numbers, booleans, calendar dates and shape; invalid entries are counted and never rounded or silently converted, invalid persisted data blocks edits rather than being overwritten, raw JSON export is available for recovery, cross-tab changes block saves until reload, spreadsheet formula injection is mitigated on CSV export, and the bounded import size was raised to 20 MB so the 5,000-entry schema can import its own backups. Its former clinical 'improving/worsening' classifier and calendar-based advice were removed on the grounds that sparse logs should not reassure someone or postpone assessment, and the summary is now descriptive only. Validation reports 8 Node unit tests and 31 Chromium browser tests passing, automated axe WCAG 2 A/AA and 2.1 AA checks passing on all ten pages at 390px and 1440px, and no page-level horizontal overflow at 320, 390, 768 or 1440px. Sources retrieved 2026-09-20.
flags: Its own verification policy refuses the strongest claims a directory reader might assume: 'Unknown or conflicting facts stay visibly unresolved. No claim of independent clinical verification or zero errors', and 'Automated checks cannot establish medical accuracy'. REVIEW.md adds that no clinician independently reviewed the personalised suitability of the information, and that link integrity, automated accessibility and browser tests are not medical validation.

Deliberately narrower than the version it replaced. The prior revision carried a 56-source register (S1-S56), four logged review passes, 32 logged corrections and a 32-row irregularity table; this one carries 20 opened sources, three passes, 8 source irregularities and a 6-row next-steps table. Its stated reason is worth quoting because it is the opposite of the usual instinct: 'The guide is a focused, source-linked starting set, not all possible diseases or products. Further expansion should improve evidence rather than inflate a count' (IRR-57).

Now has a build and test step, unlike the version previously described here: npm ci, npm run build (claim ledger plus ten static root HTML pages), npm run check, npm test, npm run test:browser (Playwright) and npm run serve, with the shared page layout in tools/build.py and Python 3 and Node 22 used in validation. Visitors need neither. Committed root HTML means the Pages configuration needs no runtime build.

Browser tests were run against an npm-distributed Chromium 153 binary extracted outside Git because the standard Playwright browser download and Debian package retrieval were blocked by sandbox networking; REVIEW.md states plainly that 'this is not an unexecuted test claim', and CI uses the normal Playwright installation on GitHub-hosted runners. Remaining testing limits it names: no manual screen-reader-user audit, no cross-browser matrix, no third-party video-playback test, and automated accessibility is not full conformance certification.

Open limitations it lists for a next session: no clinician exam or clinical peer review and no systematic literature review; actual room fit, safe removal route and body/desk measurements unknown; no checked chair meets both the folding and the adjustable long-day-workstation criteria; product stock, prices and return policies change and Lillipad has contradictory page content; personal care and medicine costs, country and insurance remain unknown.

Changed state four times inside one audit and this description is the fourth rewrite — verified in sequence against 239eaa8 (01:25:47Z), dd1a7d4 (02:13:17Z), 6812ef3 (02:42:19Z, 60 seconds after a prior stamp had been written) and now 8a21b94 (03:07:51Z), which rebuilt all ten pages and reversed the sourcing method entirely (IRR-47, IRR-57).

Re-verified upstream on 21 September 2026: every medical, exercise and workstation source (M1-M6, E1-E3, W1-W3) was re-opened and all registered excerpts still match the official pages. Product rechecks succeeded only partially — VIVO and Lillipad were re-verified through official seller product-data endpoints, while fetch-proxy failures prevented re-opening IKEA, Branch, three manual/spec PDFs and the cost sources, whose entries stay dated 20 September 2026 and are labelled as such on the site. No price, stock or fit fact was invented for the items that could not be re-opened.

VacationSchedule.title: VacationSchedule — Free Time Scoreboard (SF Radio Blackout Calendar)
VacationSchedule.description: Bay Area vacation planner comparing three definitions of sports-free time in 2026-2029 for a listener in San Francisco ZIP 94122, with one-, two- and three-week trip checks, a daily scoreboard, a month calendar, Pacific-time free intervals, sources and a review queue. The three sections nest: Section 1 counts all 30 MLB clubs plus 49ers preseason, regular season and postseason and the Westwood One national NFL feeds as busy; Section 2 adds Stanford and California football; Section 3 adds San Jose Earthquakes MLS. An 'Everything tracked' option adds national NCAA football plus Golden State Warriors and Golden State Valkyries on KGMZ 95.7 The Game. Only AM/FM broadcasts count, so the San Jose Sharks (app/streaming only) and Audacy-app-only Valkyries games are disclosed exclusions, and USF basketball, Westwood One NCAA basketball and local college basketball are named as documented gaps rather than silently treated as free time. With Spring Training excluded, Sections 1 and 2 give longest modeled windows of 44 days in 2026 (Feb 9 - Mar 24, past), 37 in 2027 (Feb 15 - Mar 23), 40 in 2028 (estimated) and 41 in 2029 (estimated); with Spring Training included no section reaches two weeks. The repository refuses a blanket verified claim: TBD kickoff reserves the entire local date including DST 23- and 25-hour days, 'no known conflict' is stated to describe the snapshot rather than certify a quiet day, and all times are America/Los_Angeles rather than a fixed UTC-8 offset. A 2026-09-21 session-3 pass added two tabs: MLB 2026 & 2027, listing every fixture the league has scheduled for all 30 clubs from the committed Stats API snapshot with each row carrying the league's own game_pk, and Postseason 2026, which splits the postseason into what is resolved and what is not — clinched berths and division titles, official round dates, dates that cannot carry a game, and a machine-measured count of published first pitches, still zero. The fixture lists are produced on a GitHub runner by scripts/export_mlb_schedule.py, validated for all 30 clubs, a plausible regular-season count and unique game ids, and committed with a provenance summary recording the exact request URL, the retrieval time and a SHA-256 of the raw response, so every row is re-verifiable by hand. Where a season snapshot exists the analysis blocks real fixture dates rather than a continuous season frame. The 125-test suite was executed here and passes.

NBAComp.title: NBAComp — Autonomous NBA Betting Strategy Research & Paper-Trading Competition
NBAComp.description: Autonomous NBA betting-strategy research and paper-trading competition lab that cross-verifies real public data, turns public claims into testable hypotheses, backtests them against verified historical prices where those exist and forward-tests them where they do not. It runs 27 system-generated strategies (NBA-001 through NBA-027) with a $1,000 virtual bankroll each over a competition window of 2026-09-20 to 2027-09-19, staking at 25% Kelly capped at 3% per bet, collecting ESPN schedule, scores and current odds, the ESPN injury board, Kalshi public market data and NBA.com/stats team and player logs, and modeling chronological Elo (MOV-adjusted, with season carryover), rolling pace and efficiency totals and rest, back-to-back, road-trip and time-zone features. Signal-quality results are published as signal quality and never mixed into backtest or forward PnL records. NFLComp.title: NFLComp — Autonomous NFL Betting Strategy Research & Competition
NFLComp.description: Autonomous NFL betting-strategy research, backtesting, forward-testing and paper-trading competition platform, explicitly a paper-trading research prototype rather than a production betting system. State read from the repository's own data/summary.json at commit 7ec80df: 70 strategy personas across 17 categories, 23 of them carrying a version lineage and every one flat-staking a $10,000 paper bankroll; 7,548 tracked games of which 7,308 are completed and 240 upcoming, spanning 1999 to 2026 with the current week at 3 of the 2026 season; a simulated ledger of 97,218 wagers carrying a total competition simulated PnL of -$531,192.71 (a net loss across all personas), 646 upcoming bets and 326 open positions; and 16,343 Kalshi trade prints of which 1,463 are published on the site. The published ledger window is 2020-2026, holding 31,502 bets at -$221,808.53, against the all-time 97,218 bets at -$531,192.71. The top performer is now @AnalyticsCoach_ATS_v1 at +$3,839.32 and a +4.16% ROI; @AltSpread_Value_v2, which this directory's previous entry named as the top persona at +27.15% ROI and +$145,992.37, now shows 0 bets and is listed as n/a (open) in the forward-test column, so that claim is superseded rather than carried. Strategy development is the declared main loop and is quoted from the README: declare the hypothesis, required source fields, market, side and threshold in code before reading the holdout result; develop on 2000-2019, validate on 2020-2022 and evaluate once on a 2023-2025 holdout without threshold tuning; keep failures archived unchanged; and promote only to prospective paper testing when the gate passes — at least 100 development, 40 validation and 40 holdout bets with positive ROI in all three windows — because, as the README puts it, a positive holdout is not a profit guarantee. The 33-control audit was executed here and all 33 pass.

NHLComp.title: NHLComp — Autonomous NHL Betting Strategy Research Platform
NHLComp.description: Autonomous NHL betting-strategy research and paper-trading competition platform that never trades real money: it cross-verifies real public data (official NHL schedule, boxscores, stats, rosters, drafts and standings; ESPN injury data; Kalshi public market data and, optionally, TBD one), runs backtest and forward phases with a 1,000 USD starting bankroll, a configurable 100-bet rolling window and a promotion gate requiring at least 100 backtest, 40 validation and 40 forward bets, and publishes every flag, limitation, irregularity, source and finding on the site. The leaderboard reports 83 strategies per mode with 66 active in each (17 quarantined), of which 22 show at least one settled backtest bet. The generated competition.json at 2026-09-23T02:03:46Z records the BACKTEST phase as 3,921 bets, all 3,921 settled (1,846 wins, 2,075 losses), +$1,012.43 on $122,873.96 staked — a 0.82 percent return on stakes and a 47.08 percent win rate — while the FORWARD TEST phase records 0 bets, 0 settled, 0 open and a PnL of 0.0 with a null ROI. IRREGULARITY: the same repository's data/bets.json holds 127 FORWARD TEST rows at this head, every one of them result OPEN with pnl null, so the forward zero-bet figure is a bookkeeping artifact of the forward ledger not the competition.json roll-up, and the leaderboard's forward rows additionally carry 1 preseason settled bet worth +$53.26 that is explicitly flagged scored_in_competition false (IRR-99). A hockey-specific tracker (scripts/nhl_track.py --analyze) runs the 66 active strategies against the 2025-26 season as the forward book; the leaderboard's quality block reports 94 irregularities registered, 83 published (26 open, 68 resolved) and 167 findings and 30 sources, while a separate independent verifier at commit 3456621 re-validated 5,248 team-game rows against the official schedule with 0 score conflicts (392 of them shootout-adjusted) and 7,968 totals settlement contracts with 0 conflicts.

SocialMediaComp.title: SocialMediaComp — High-Reach Social Accounts Leaderboard

Every entry carries an id, platform, handle, owner, topic, metric label and value, a snapshot note, the profile URL, the source name and URL, growth notes, a verified-list flag, cohort, country, likes in billions and the batch it arrived in. The verification rule is stated in data/master-list.json itself: every follower, member or subscriber figure is taken from a cited source fetched in the session shown in docs/VERIFICATION.md, and nothing is taken from a summary that was not itself read. MLBRainDelay.title: MLB Rain Delay — Live Scoreboard with Weather & Delay Tracking
MLBRainDelay.description: Dependency-free static MLB rain-delay and postponement tracker and research site that cross-references the public MLB StatsAPI schedule with official NWS point, hourly forecast and alerts JSON (or the Environment Canada equivalent for Toronto) plus a documented list of stadium roof/retractable-roof facts, and labels every game's delay risk by a published rule rather than a guess. It covers the full official gameStatus registry — all 210 status codes captured verbatim in the fixtures — maps status.detailedState / statusCode / reason to High / Moderate / Low / None / Covered / Unknown with thresholds spelled out in RISK_RULES so a reviewer can re-derive every label, and lists 13 club pages with 11 named deficiencies (warm-weather bias, no surface/drainage field, market prices no single source publishes, and so on). One mode classifies a schedule; the other reclassifies an already-observed delay or postponement and measures the retrospective recall and precision of the prospective label on committed verified delays — never the other way round — and the site states plainly that a positive calibration result is not a validated operational delay-forecasting model. The social/headline layer is explicitly a flag-for-review aid that only fires when a news headline's verbatim title or description contains a word from the documented DELAY_WORDS / WEATHER_WORDS lists, recording the matched word, and it never asserts a delay. IRREGULARITY: the repository's own test suites have grown past the figures its documentation still prints. Executed here with node: tools/delays-test.mjs 32 passed, tools/weather-test.mjs 25 passed and tools/render-test.mjs 9 passed (66 across the three suites this entry's previous version named), with tools/news-test.mjs 25 passed and tools/match-test.mjs 18 passed also green — while docs/verification.md still reports '67 assertions across four suites (26 + 24 + 11 + 6)' and README.md still reports '100+ passing assertions' (IRR-103).

By design it does not scan Twitter/X, Facebook, Instagram, Reddit or news sites — the repository states a keyless static page has no verifiable way to read them — and instead links official club news, @MLB_PR, NWS and SPC pages under a Manual review heading. Its own Limitations section also records that browser CORS for the Environment Canada endpoint is still unverified and that some special-event venues have no coordinates.

SelfLearn.title: SelfLearn — Autonomous No-LLM Research Engine
SelfLearn.description: An autonomous, offline-first research engine: six numbered sources (arXiv, Crossref, GitHub, NIST NVD, PyPI, USGS), eleven named deterministic critic rules, nine published scoring criteria, a contradiction register that is never silently resolved, and a CLI that serves, publishes, re-verifies and reports. README.md at commit c492159 describes the pipeline as Compete (six personas build candidate answers made only of quotations plus fixed scaffolding), Criticise (eleven named rules attack each candidate, each attack recording the rule that fired) and Refuse when a source cannot be quoted. The generated run-a467fa87a6df site data (2026-09-23T00:55:17Z) reports 300 claims, 93 documents, 222 competing candidates carrying 960 recorded criticisms, 147 derived open questions, 12 contradictions awaiting a human decision, 102 discoveries, 4 topics, 5 experiments, 28 failures and 46 registered irregularities (23 info, 15 warning, 0 error) of which 38 are open and 8 resolved. Substance is measured rather than asserted: 42 of 300 claims are dated, 252 are quantified, the mean substance score is 0.5166 and 39.67 percent of the corpus is substantive rather than metadata. The run's own change scan attempted 6 sources and scanned 2: arXiv, Crossref, USGS and NVD all returned policy_refused because their robots.txt could not be fetched over the sandbox's TLS egress and RFC 9309 2.3.1.4 requires a crawler to assume complete disallow in that case, so no request was made to those hosts; GitHub and PyPI scanned and returned 13 new items between them. Its link checker reports 126 links checked, 106 ok and 20 failed, and records that the check ran on a GitHub Actions runner with unrestricted egress so that 'unreachable' is not mistaken for a broken link. Its own checks block additionally reports 159 claims without a link and 10 unsupported claims. The test suite was executed here: 189 passed.

MasterSelfLearn.title: MasterSelfLearn — Autonomous Evidence-First Research Engine
MasterSelfLearn.description: Autonomous, evidence-first research engine that runs on a timer with no manual input: .github/workflows/think.yml fires on a */30 * * * * cron, reads official public data, appends to a claims ledger, regenerates the site and documentation and commits its own output, so a cycle that reads nothing still publishes and says so. A cycle is seven stages, each a separate module that can fail without stopping the others — a failed stage becomes an entry in the irregularity register and the cycle still publishes. Figures below are the repository's own regenerated AUTO:COUNTS block at commit 86cb822, cycle 25, generated 2026-09-23T01:42:26Z: 22,070 accepted claims in the ledger (6,963 under the schema-v2 strict trace contract and 15,107 under the legacy contract reported but not upgraded; 14,570 captured from accepted source reads, 7,477 derived by recorded arithmetic and 23 negative proofs of absence), 0 claims rejected by the evidence gate, 2,294 derived claims rechecked this cycle with 0 that no longer recompute, 163 topics in the library (6 new), 416 published insights, 1,110 forecasts issued this cycle and 655 scored against outcomes, 28 ideas in the competition with 1 promoted, 27 open irregularities (1 new), 31 registered sources of which 28 are verified by a recorded live read and 3 are currently blocked, 63 reads ok against 4 failed this cycle out of 67 planned with 0 refused by the cap, 3,346 forecasts waiting for an observation, 0 that can never be scored, 2,155,278 bytes read, and 0 manual inputs required. data/irregularities.json at the same timestamp records 123 irregularities registered in total — 6 critical, 72 warn and 45 info — of which 27 are open, 96 resolved and 21 standing, where standing means a structural limit that deliberately does not auto-resolve. The 350-test suite was executed in this audit and passed (350 passed in 13.40s).

Coupons.title: Coupons — Bay Area Verified Product Coupons
Coupons.description: Product-only coupon, rebate and BOGO directory for the San Francisco Bay Area, re-scoped on 2026-09-22 to drop event tickets and museum admissions (49 venue-admission entries moved to archive/rescoped-2026-09-22/ with their reasoning, per the dataset's own scope_history). State read from the repository's own generated data/coupons.json at commit 7a130e1 (built_at 2026-09-22T23:43:31Z): 227 verified offers, 20 documented rejections, 265 citations across 72 distinct source domains, verification levels A 190 / B 34 / C 3, and 613 irregularity flags (20 critical, 497 warning, 96 info). Offers live in 15 curated JSON shards under data/entries/ — the largest, 01-pg-brandsaver.json, holding 112 transcribed P&G brandSAVER coupons — and carry 13 deal types. Sourcing is enforced by the build, not by convention: an aggregator, promo-code site, listicle or social domain cited as the source of an available offer fails the build, as does a citation with no verbatim evidence passage, publisher, access date and retrieval method. Expiry status is computed in the browser against the visitor's own date (Active to Expires soon at 7 days or fewer, to Expired, plus Window closed and Not redeemable yet), and every dated record carries a project-side recheck_due date set to the printed expiry minus a 3-day safety margin, which a weekly CI job uses to file re-verification issues before an offer goes stale. The suite now reports 56 tests (53 at the previous read), executed here with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`: Ran 56 tests, OK.

FLABSENGY.title: FLABSENGY — FantasyLabs Projection Reverse Engineering
FLABSENGY.description: Clean-room study of the FantasyLabs DFS projection system plus an original Python engine that rebuilds the metrics the vendor documents publicly — no subscription data, no scraped pages, no proprietary weights, and an explicit record of what was refused. Evidence counted at commit f927bab: docs/ledger.html holds 49 source rows inside an S1-S50 range, research/IRREGULARITIES.md carries 16 flagged items I1-I16, research/REQUIREMENTS.md maps acceptance requirements R1-R17, and engine/fantasylab_engine/metrics.py defines 14 functions covering Plus/Minus, implied points from a salary-expectation fit, Pts/Sal, consistency, upside, duds, bargain rating, opponent Plus/Minus, salary change and percentile rank. `pytest -q` was executed in this audit and returned 79 passed. Where the vendor's own official glossaries disagree — the NFL defines Duds as fewer than half a salary-based expectation while the NBA and MLB glossaries define it as at least half a standard deviation below it — the engine implements both variants and documents which one is the default; where a methodology is not public at all (ownership projection, Pro Trend definitions, salary-regression parameters) it is recorded as unknown rather than guessed.
flags: Two of the README's headline counts are off against the files they describe. Its table says '50 sources' where docs/ledger.html holds 49 rows — the ledger states in terms that 'Missing ID S15 is reserved (not used)' — and 'All 19 publicly documented metrics' where docs/metrics.html carries 20 metric rows. This entry publishes the counted values 49 and 20; the disagreement is IRR-74.

The refusals are the substance of the audit, not an omission from it: I1-I3 record that the request to rebuild whatever sits behind the paywall would be paywall circumvention and reproduction of copyrighted subscription content, and that the Terms governing fantasylabs.com ban scraping, robots and reverse engineering of source code. The repository therefore limited itself to a handful of direct public page reads and wrote the engine from published metric definitions.

Two live findings about the vendor are reported and deliberately not exploited: fantasylabs.com/articles-new/ is publicly reachable and labelled '(Test)' in a search index (I10), and a search index surfaced a raw JSON player-news API path that appeared to need no authentication (I11). The endpoint was not interrogated further and is not consumed.

FanDuel scoring is taken from the operator's own rules page against secondary DFS guides that claim FanDuel has no yardage bonuses (I12); the engine trusts official pages only and excludes the secondary tables from its config.

FUTURESCOMMODITIES.title: FUTURESCOMMODITIES — Commodity Futures Paper-Trading Competition
FUTURESCOMMODITIES.description: Live engine, one strategy roster, twenty explicit instruments and one venue family, with no simulation anywhere. engine/strategies/index.mjs registers exactly 20 strategies and usernames: 9 Kalshi event contracts, 2 Kalshi perpetuals, 5 exchange commodity futures (MOEX FORTS), 1 FX, 1 equity index, 1 interest-rate and 1 cross-venue instrument, each with its declared data source, granularity, time horizon, risk model and sizing rule. config/competition.json fixes the season window 2026-09-22 to 2027-09-22, a $100,000 starting bankroll, 130 ms between engine ticks, a 12-hour history refresh, a 100-series candle cap, taker fills at 25% of visible depth, a 6-hour maker TTL and 0.001 perp participation, with MOEX gates at 10-minute volume, 20-minute open interest, 2% price and 5% open interest. data/reports/summary.json (2026-09-23T00:52:33Z) reports the first live run: 5 ticks, the last with 1,900 instruments, 107 quotes, 26 trades, 3 intents, 181 requests and 0 settlements, with all 20 leaderboard rows equity_complete true at $100,000.00 — an opening equity of 99,839.83, -0.16% — 13 of them carrying open positions and 0 closed trades, 0 fees and 0 slippage. data/verification/report.json checks 132 trades against the official APIs: 98 fully verified, 34 anomalies (28 instrument-universe, 6 cross-venue basis), across 107 instruments (45 kalshi, 12 kalshi_margin, 50 moex_forts), with fill tiers 94 quote-based, 38 ladder and 0 modelled maker. data/reports/backtests.json records 6 backtests and 817 simulated trades, of which moex-metals-trend-10d carries 674 at -9.4448% and moex-metal-breakout-20-10 carries 143 at -4.5481% while the four Kalshi runs each ran 0 trades; 4 strategies are marked unavailable_for_backtesting. MOEX fees are quoted at ISS USD/RUB 84.72 and the repo discloses no depth, slippage or participation model.
flags: Catalog and competition state disagree because the repository moved while it was being read. Commit a64a347 ('Expand to 17 strategies, re-enable cross-venue basis on verified contract data, add research backtests and live-desk/research site sections', 2026-09-22T23:04:47Z) added five strategies and re-enabled @basis-hunter, but the tick it sits on top of was generated at 23:03:54Z and still reports coverage.strategies == 12 with a 12-row leaderboard. Both numbers are published here with the file each came from instead of being reconciled. IRR-75.

All 10 verification anomalies are the same check, instrument_present_in_published_universe — instruments that settled and dropped out of the universe file. They are reported on the site and never silently corrected.

Of the 6 documented backtest rules only two recorded any trades at all (Metals Settlement Trend 674 and Channel Breakout 20/10 on MOEX metals 143); the other four recorded 0. The 817 total is the sum of total_trades_recorded across the six, and the file's own caveat states that a backtest 'is never a track record and never a season trade'. Its fills are at published daily prices with no depth, no slippage, no participation cap and no queue position.

Where an exchange blocks scripted access — CME Group, ICE, LME, Eurex, JPX, SGX, B3 — contract specifications are cited from official pages but no price is simulated, and the strategy is labelled unavailable for backtesting rather than filled from a proxy.

This is a returns-only simulator by design: strategies are deliberately not risk-managed because the competition is scored on returns alone, and the only hard constraints are real liquidity from the published order books and a one-position-per-instrument rule.

LSTARENGY.title: LSTARENGY — Evidence-Led Sports Projection Research
LSTARENGY.description: Evidence-led research into LineStar's DFS projection product (linestarapp.com): a dated review of the vendor's own public product descriptions, an independent data-and-implementation plan, and a runnable projection prototype over synthetic data. The repository states in terms what it is not — not a recovered private algorithm, not a subscription bypass, not a production sports-data service, not a legal clearance and not a demonstrated match to LineStar's data quality — and its research snapshot is dated 2026-09-22 UTC with the note that build dates do not reset source observation dates. Every count here was read from the committed evidence register at 66d9c9b and re-confirmed by running the repository's own validator: 36 capability records (public claim, evidence references, sport and screen scope, access status, independent implementation status, required inputs, limitations), 30 source records distinguishing vendor, league, government, provider, platform and community-maintainer, each with an observation date, short excerpt, location, link and excerpt hash; 62 line-referenced legacy claim groups correcting the previous state of this repository against the immutable base commit 0ac0b07a; a 13-label coverage plan, nine input categories, 14 review flags, 10 findings and six prioritized next-work packages. `npm run check` was executed in this audit and passed all three of its gates: `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` reported 72 tests, 72 pass, 0 fail on Node v22.22.3; `scripts/validate.mjs` printed 'Traceability valid: 36 capabilities, 30 sources, 62 legacy review groups. This is not automated proof of source truth.'; and `scripts/build.mjs --check` printed 'Verified 22 deterministic site assets. Both main:/ and main:/docs entrypoints are supported.' A further 13 Playwright browser and accessibility specs exist in tests/browser/ and were not executed, because no browser binary is available in this audit environment. The published site is a 217,302-byte root index.html built from web/template.html with search, category and evidence filtering, deep citations, JSON and CSV downloads and no-JavaScript research content; the prototype is a deterministic lab doing recency-weighted mean forecasts, point-in-time filtering, historical quantiles, an exact small-pool lineup solver, locks and exclusions, optional QB stack, greedy multi-lineup diversity and exposure constraints, late-swap slot preservation, stale-data blocking and safe CSV export, evaluated walk-forward on fixtures with EV arithmetic from assumed rather than estimated probabilities. All lab athlete labels, scores, salaries, odds and event dates are test fixtures. The build, validator, unit tests and demo have no runtime package dependencies and need no network or credentials. The repository is 60 tracked files.

The bankrolls have nevertheless moved, and the two readings do not agree: sum(starting_bankroll) is 10,001,606.66 against sum(current_bankroll) of 9,919,682.37, a difference of -81,924.29 or -0.82 percent of the capital started, while the per-user total_pnl field that a reader would take for the result reads 0.00 everywhere. This directory publishes both and resolves neither (IRR-89). The strategy library is 52 programs across six categories (game-based 11, situational 11, market-based 10, prop-based 10, correlation 5, statistical 5), up from 37 at the previous head. verification_report.json, generated 2026-09-22T23:42:21Z, reports valid true with 577 UNVERIFIED_DATA flags and no MISSING_DATA flag at all: the market manifest it reported missing an hour earlier now exists, with 6 rows, 0 malformed and valid true. The repository still states that no verified market data has been collected — data/raw/ is absent from the committed tree — and each flag gives the reason per trade ('Market file missing for KXNFLGAME-26SEP21LVPHI, may be synthetic fixture'). The published site is still reached through a root index.html forwarder into docs/, now accompanied by a .nojekyll file at the root to stop Jekyll processing the legacy Pages build, and docs/site_data/ holds 1,057 files totalling 6.44 MB. The Kalshi fee schedule transcribed into the engine and asserted by its tests is unchanged across this range — no file under engine/ or tests/ was touched between 84f138f and fef877f — so the result executed at the previous head carries: Ran 103 tests, OK with 1 skipped, with scripts/test_all.py reporting all four gates passed. Taker fees round up(M x 0.07 x C x P x (1-P)) and are charged at execution with no settlement fee, maker fees are M x 0.0175, the KXNFLGAME multiplier is 1, and NFL combos are maker 2 / taker 1.

ParlaySports.title: ParlaySports — Multi-Sport Parlay Paper Competition
ParlaySports.description: Simulated multi-sport parlay research platform and paper-trading competition across NFL, MLB, NHL and NBA — dependency-free Python engine, hash-routed static site, two sealed books that are accounted separately and never merged. State read from data/site/meta.json at commit f939267 (engine 1.1.0, exported 2026-09-22T20:06:21Z over data as of 2026-09-22T01:30:00Z): 29,056 games, 7,014 parlays, 20,570 legs and the same 20,570 signals, 8,267 ledger rows, 60,504 prices, 54,296 ratings, 28 strategies, 28 users, 24 research items, 28 verifications and 13 open quality issues. The catalog in parlaysports/strategies.py is 28 versioned strategies — six per sport plus four multi-sport — each with a named manager, a written hypothesis, selection rules, a minimum edge and documented limitations, staking 10 USD per ticket (the longshot lottery book 25 USD) from a 10,000 USD bankroll per strategy per book. Every leg and ticket carries a pricing grade: VERIFIED, REFERENCE, MODEL, MIXED or UNPRICED, the last tracked for hit rate only at 0 stake. Settlement is append-only from final scores, with push and void legs reducing a ticket and an all-push ticket refunded. Three gates were executed in this audit rather than quoted: the unittest suite ran 60 tests OK, the committed data/audit_report.json holds 63 checks every one of which is PASS, and node scripts/ui_smoke.mjs rendered all 15 site routes.
flags: The committed audit report is 63/63 PASS, but re-running scripts/audit.py from a fresh clone in this audit stopped at check 2 with 'database-exists: run seed first', because the working database is not committed. The 63/63 published here is the repository's own persisted record at this commit, not a gate this audit reproduced end to end; `make seed` has to run first. IRR-78.

Coverage gaps are declared rather than padded: the pinned MLB results file holds full 2023-2025 and Apr-Jul 2015 only, with nothing for 2016-2022, so MLB backtests run over 2023-2025 and a missing-historical-periods quality check flags the gap on every build. NBA backtests use Oct-Dec slices only from the SBR archive, S-NHL-05 has no verified puck-line history and is forward-armed only, S-MLB-06 is forward-only by design, and multi-sport backtests cover only measured cross-sport overlap slates.

MODEL-grade payouts are estimates from assumed -110 or proxy lines and are labelled as such; backtests assume closing-line availability and ignore line movement, limits and fees; multi-sport legs assume independence with no correlation model and there are no same-game parlays in v1; Kalshi prices exclude exchange fees; and player and game props are not simulated at all because no free verified historical prop feed exists.

Twelve inherited NBA rows were 0-0 'finals' for games that had been postponed: nine are verified against published postponement notices and three are recorded as not played with verified=0 and an explicit 'reason NOT independently verified' note. Postponed games are never settled and never rated, and a ticket leg on one is voided with its stake refunded.

A flat-stake book can exceed its starting bankroll on paper, which the repository states rather than hides: equity curves, drawdowns and bankroll reconciliation are computed in economic time from ledger amounts, and the integrity checks fail the run on a negative balance, a drawdown above 100 percent or any drift against the recorded current amount.

RGENGY.title: RGENGY — RotoGrinders Data Quality Audit
RGENGY.description: Open, auditable rebuild of the data quality behind RotoGrinders' DFS projection system: what it uses, where that data comes from, what could be verified from official sources and — equally — what could not. At commit d758f87 the README's own generated statistics block reads audit date 2026-09-22, 460 tests passing, 16 registered endpoints, 11 scoring tables and 34 findings on the register, and each of those was independently re-counted in this audit: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` ran 460 tests OK, rgengy/data/scoring/ holds 11 JSON tables (MLB across DraftKings, FanDuel and Yahoo, NBA, NFL, NHL and WNBA across DraftKings and FanDuel), rgengy/findings.py carries 28 IR-nn irregularities plus 6 L-nn limitations, and `python3 -m rgengy sources` prints 16 endpoints, 14 official, 2 unofficial, 0 requiring auth. The headline result is an external validation: RGENGY's independently sourced DraftKings MLB coefficients, applied to RotoGrinders' own published stat projections, reproduce the published FPTS for all 6 free rows within 0.07 FPTS (0.56 percent worst case), and FPTS per dollar reproduces exactly as FPTS / (SALARY / 1000) with a maximum error of 0.0036 over those 6 rows — the only RotoGrinders analytic column the project claims to reproduce. Counting the tables value by value, 122 coefficients across 9 of the 11 carry confirmed_by_operator true. Anything that could not be verified is null with a written reason: RotoGrinders' OBFPTS, TOPVAL, DIFFERENCE, OPTO and TEAMOWN columns have no published formula.

StokEngineer.title: StokEngineer — Stokastic Reverse Engineering
StokEngineer.description: Zero-network, dependency-free DFS projection and optimizer rebuild of Stokastic's public methodology, self-contained and re-runnable offline, that separates official sources (DraftKings scoring rules, FanDuel, MLB Stats API, nflverse, NBA stats endpoints), reverse-engineered vendor methodology and independent analysis, and ships its own multi-sport projection engine: src/projection_engine/ holds 8 modules — data_sources, nba_projections, nfl_projections, mlb_projections, ownership_model, boom_bust, top_stacks and simulation_engine — with a deterministic optimizer that adds a stack constraint, ownership leverage, diversity, exposure and what-if lineups to the base knobs. The project's honest boundary is explicit: Stokastic's exact projection weights, sigma model and ownership coefficients are not public, so nothing claims them. VERIFICATION.md at commit 7dedfea is an 89-line document describing the mechanism rather than the 24-line claim log it was at the previous read, and the machine-readable claim log now lives in src/data/claims.json, which holds 25 claims (19 verified, 5 flagged, 1 not_verified). src/data/sources_verified.json is the machine-readable source registry: 29 sources (13 fetched_live in session, 5 github_api, 11 carried_over and explicitly treated as unverified) plus 4 removed_or_downgraded, and src/stokengineer/provenance.py refuses to use a source id that is not in it while tools/check_links.py re-walks every URL. The previous version of this entry published '38 source entries across six categories', '155 verified badges' and 'a 24-line claim log'; none of those figures, nor the 71,004-byte site or the 7 flagged irregularities it also cited, is re-derivable from the current tree.

PRICINGEXPERT.title: PRICINGEXPERT — Kalshi Paper-Trading Competition & Research Desk
PRICINGEXPERT.description: Autonomous live book-maker lab for prediction markets, focused on pricing theory rather than profit: it builds a public-data-only order-book model for Kalshi contracts (books, candles, schedules, settlements, market metadata, series and fees) and models the three things a bookmaker must decide — the fair price, the price to quote and the price at which to stop quoting. The model assumes an order-flow process whose initial estimate of the fair value is wrong, models the informed side as having observed the outcome while the uninformed side is noisy, states a pure market-maker objective of capturing the spread, and prices an American binary option by valuing the asset at exercise and converting to an event probability through the inverse CDF — the midpoint between the bid and the ask is a price, not an expectation. It publishes a scoring guide for spread captures (a continuous book with depth at every price scores a capture, a depleted or one-sided book scores a price change, a stale book scores no capture), a venue-analysis guide framed as mid-price precision and a mirror-fill cost, a 61-category research log with the explicit caveat that a category is a hypothesis class rather than a conclusion, and a stated limit that thin books inflate Kelly fractions and that public-data candles are not always printable. data/candles/ holds 84 committed candle files (53 KXBTC, 31 KXETHD) from 12 series, including every contract month under the KXBTCD and KXETHD series with official fetch provenance, and data/manifest.json's series-catalog entry is a 17,505,797-byte full series catalog with volume, sha256 af04b45aabd739cd0d3f78d782b327cdb72e7c23e6300e45566319d2da28. The competition has not traded: data/season-2026/forward/leaderboard.json reports cycles_completed 0 with 10 strategies all still at $10,000.00, realized_pnl 0.0 and 0 fills, and data/season-2026/forward/{trades,intents,marks}.jsonl are each 0 lines. scripts/verify.py was executed here and reports passed 1198, errors 0 (its checks array lists 12 V1/V2 messages phrased as the failures they did not find, so the string 'missing provenance' in that output means the opposite), and `python3 -m pytest tests -q` reports 39 passed. A new data/season-2026/backtest/results.json records a candle-replay backtest that states its own assumptions in the artifact: signal on bar t close, fill at bar t+1 open with no look-ahead, candle-proxied touches that are explicitly NOT book-verified, a default 2-cent limit buffer capped at 0.99, cumulative-volume gates and signed slippage.

A leaderboard of ten personas all sitting on exactly $10,000.00 is a season that has not started, not a competition with no winners. Every figure in this entry comes from the repository's own committed data files at a61a2eb.

The verification gate passes but is only half exercised, and the way it reports is a trap for a reader. `check(ok, code, msg)` in scripts/verify.py appends msg to CHECKS when ok is True and to ERRORS when it is False, and every msg is phrased as the failure it did not find — so the printed `passed: 42` sits next to lines reading 'V1: hash mismatch exchange-status.json' and 'V13-trades: duplicate rows detected', which look like 42 failures and are 42 passes. `errors: 0` with exit code 0 is the authoritative signal. V12 (link well-formedness) has no pass path at all — it calls check() only on a placeholder URL — so a clean link audit contributes nothing to either list, and remote reachability is CI-only via scripts/probe_links.py.

scripts/verify.py is not read-only: it writes data/site/link-audit.json as a side effect. Run in a clean clone it left `git status` empty, so the rewrite was byte-identical to the committed file — deterministic, and worth knowing before running it inside a working tree you care about.

The repository registers its own irregularities, in the same spirit as this directory: data/site/verification.json carries 3, recording that direct HTTPS from its build sandbox cannot reach api.elections.kalshi.com (SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL on connect while DNS resolves), so evidence collection went through the platform's server-side fetch route with the tool used recorded in each provenance sidecar; that this proxy failed intermittently with server-side OSS errors (InvalidAccessKeyId on the proxy's own storage); and that the CandleCharts contest page was cited from the project brief and a search result but not fully retrieved. Its evidence is therefore genuine but brokered, and it says so.

Per the repository's README (session 9, 2026-09-17): the three official competition rasters are now committed as sha256-pinned git parts under data/bridge/ and reassembled into data/. This is a deliberate design choice, but '384 MB of rasters in git' is the kind of growth that runs into GitHub's repository size guidance (soft warning at ~5 GB, 100 MB per-file warning) and makes clones slow. Suggest Git LFS or a release asset instead.

irregularities.title: TinoLunchSpecial size fell 4,864 KB -> 2,076 KB across 12 new commits
irregularities.detail: The first commit SHA is unchanged (c7bd9eb, 2026-09-07T19:05:24Z), so this is file removal in ordinary commits rather than a history rewrite. GitHub recomputes the size field asynchronously, so part of the delta may be accounting lag rather than deleted bytes.

irregularities.title: NFLInjuryReport size fell 6,246 KB -> 5,855 KB across 7 new commits
irregularities.detail: Same pattern as IRR-05: first commit SHA unchanged (5d8a07f), seven new main-branch commits, net size reduction.

irregularities.title: GitHub's three timestamp fields do not always agree with each other
irregularities.detail: Observed at the 2026-09-17 snapshot, measured from GitHub's own fields: GEMSDOE pushed_at (2026-09-17T21:42:44Z) is ~2.4 h later than its newest main commit (8f7fc51, 19:21:20Z) because of arena/* session branch activity, while its updated_at (19:21:26Z) sits ~2.4 h BEFORE pushed_at. ScheduleFreeTime pushed_at (21:42:58Z) is 215 s later than its newest main commit (cdef1db, 21:39:23Z) and its updated_at (21:39:28Z) is 210 s before pushed_at. Tradingview-pinescript-editor updated_at (2026-08-19T04:53:13Z) is ~9.1 days later than its pushed_at (2026-08-10T01:43:17Z); Itinerary-Korea is ~7.8 h later and HotelSeoulRoughdraft1 ~6.2 h. Note that NBAInjuryReport showed pushed_at 97 s EARLIER than its newest main commit earlier in the same audit and had resolved to +6 s by the final read — these fields are eventually consistent, not transactionally consistent. This directory publishes created / firstCommit / lastCommit / pushedAt / updatedAt separately rather than picking one, because each answers a different question.

irregularities.title: One repository is intentionally and permanently omitted from this directory
irregularities.detail: The account holds 45 public GitHub Pages repositories; this directory publishes 44 entries. One repository was removed by owner request on 2026-09-12 and is suppressed from data/sites.js, the README counts, the audit ledger and the JSON/CSV exports. This gap is deliberate — do not re-add it to 'restore' the counts. See AGENTS.md. (Counts updated 2026-09-20; this entry previously read 39/38 and 41/40 on earlier audits.)

irregularities.title: Live *.github.io pages could not be re-fetched over HTTP from the audit sandbox
irregularities.detail: Network egress from the audit environment reaches github.com / api.github.com but not buffedlizard55-lab.github.io (DNS resolves, connection fails; the same restriction blocks example.com). Site liveness is therefore evidenced by two API facts — Pages status 'built' from GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pages, and a real index.html at the published path from the contents API — not by an HTTP 200 on the rendered page. Every entry still links to its live site for manual review.

irregularities.title: Five entries are README/documentation renders rather than applications
irregularities.detail: Leg3SeoulTrip, NFLPRED and VacationSchedule contain only a single short README.md (15, 9 and 18 bytes respectively), so Pages serves the default Jekyll markdown render with no site code. MLB-Prediction-model-backtest and PFFNFL publish their project documentation while the actual software is Python that runs locally. All five are labelled stubs in the directory. (Rewritten 2026-09-20: an earlier version of this entry still named StockPaperSim as a single-commit stub after it had become a full multi-page site — the IRR-25 error — and Elections has since grown from an 11-byte README into a full application, IRR-33.)

irregularities.detail: GEMSDOE publishes from main /, but the root index.html redirects to ./docs/index.html, where scripts/build_site.py generates the evidence pages (Overview, Data, Metric, Method, Results, Sources, Reproduce). irregularities.detail: The automated Kalshi price-history collector and backtester is a server-side Python/SQLite/Parquet service (docker compose up or ./scripts/run_autonomous.sh), built on the live engine from karagemop466-tech/Kalshi and ported into server/ + docs/. irregularities.detail: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pages/deployments returns 404 for every repository in this directory. All sites use standard branch-based Pages publishing, which does not create Actions deployment objects.

irregularities.title: MasterSite indexes itself
irregularities.detail: This repository is listed as one of its own 44 entries, so its commit count, size and last-updated timestamp move with every audit refresh — including the refresh that publishes this sentence.

irregularities.title: Descriptions are README-sourced and can go stale between refreshes
irregularities.detail: Every description is extracted from the repository's own README.md or generated site, which means a push that changes a README without changing the facts this directory records leaves the wording behind. Concrete example found on 2026-09-17: BathTubOverflowSF's 'Current research snapshot' header still reads 'Checked through September 16, 2026 / sixteen waves' while the same README documents waves 17, 18 and 19. The generator re-reads every README whose commit count moved, but prose still needs a human check. The 2026-09-18 audit found the same failure again, in four places, and it is the single largest risk to this directory: StockPaperSim was still described as a README-only placeholder after it had become a full site, KalshiPaperSim's quoted AUTO:COUNTS totals had all moved, NBAInjuryReport's test counts (188/52) no longer matched its README (212/71), and TradingViewTheLeap's README pointer named a capture file that a later capture had superseded. A numeric token still being present somewhere in a long README is not proof that a claim is current, so tools/audit_descriptions.py only narrows the search - a human or model pass has to read each one.

irregularities.title: NBAInjuryReport uses ESPN data and says so; no official NBA report was available
irregularities.detail: The site's own README states the injury board comes from ESPN's public structured injuries endpoint and is 'not official NBA confirmation', that missing listings do not mean healthy players, and that no live official NBA injury report could be discovered during the audit — automatic official confirmation stays blocked until an official page exposes report links. The 2026-09-17 snapshot names 27 of 30 team blocks (CLE, DET, LAL absent).

irregularities.title: KalshiPaperSim was rebuilt because its predecessor invented data
irregularities.detail: The repository README states it was rebuilt after an audit found the previous version invented data, and now enforces by code and tests that no price, quote, fee, market or series is invented, that no performance number is hard-coded, and that modelled data is labelled as modelled.

irregularities.title: Several repositories were still changing while the audit ran
irregularities.detail: SFWeather, ScheduleFreeTime, TradingViewTheLeap, NBAInjuryReport, KalshiPaperSim and GEMSDOE all received pushes during the audit window on 2026-09-17 — three of the four new repositories were created the same day. Commit counts and SHAs here are a point-in-time read taken at the 'generated' timestamp shown in the directory header; re-run tools/build_data.py for a fresh read. IRR-07 records how much the timestamp fields moved between two reads taken minutes apart.

irregularities.title: WoWForever existed for less than three hours when this audit read it
irregularities.detail: GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/WoWForever returned created_at 2026-09-18T20:11:30Z and the repository was still merging pull requests at 2026-09-18T22:29:32Z, so its commit total, size and last-updated fields were moving while the audit ran. It is listed here because it already satisfies every inclusion rule - public, Pages status 'built', publishing from main /, and a real index.html at the published path - but the next refresh will almost certainly show different numbers. The repository's own README dates Blizzard's launch to 4 November 2026 and deliberately publishes no class tier list, no Best-in-Slot item list and no gold-per-hour figure because the beta is capped at level 20; those omissions are the repository's stated policy, not gaps in this directory.

irregularities.title: StockPaperSim was published with a description that had become false
irregularities.detail: The 2026-09-17 audit listed StockPaperSim as 'README-only placeholder ... a single initial commit containing only a 15-byte README.md' and classified it as a stub. On 2026-09-18 GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/StockPaperSim reports 67 commits on main and size 11,956 KB, the root listing contains index.html, README.md (34 KB), data/, docs/ (16 entries), memory/, research/, scripts/, sim/ and tests/, and the README documents three separate competition runs. The entry was rewritten and its classification changed from stub to app. This is exactly the class of error the directory exists to prevent - a description that was true when it was written and is now false - and it was caught only because commit counts are re-read from the API on every audit.

irregularities.title: KalshiPaperSim's quoted AUTO:COUNTS block had moved on every figure
irregularities.detail: The 2026-09-17 entry quoted 53 verified facts, 19 flagged irregularities, 10 strategies, 9 real markets, 61 daily candlesticks and 50 automated tests. The AUTO:COUNTS block in the repository's README (regenerated by scripts/render-docs.js) now reads 99 verified facts (34 documented, 39 captured from production, 1 negative/404 evidence, 20 derived by arithmetic, 5 unexplained observations), 45 flagged irregularities, 41 strategies, 9 real markets, 10,905 captured daily candlesticks across 53 replayable markets (2025-08-15 to 2026-09-18), 112 automated tests and 13 Live Desk entrants on 62 real open contracts with captured ladders. Nine real markets and the one-year scoring calendar are the only quoted values that did not move. Because the block is machine-regenerated, any entry that quotes it will be stale on the next commit - quote it with an audit date, as this entry now does.

irregularities.title: NBAInjuryReport's published test counts no longer matched its README
irregularities.detail: The 2026-09-17 entry stated a 188-check smoke test and a 52-check integration suite. The repository's run/test block now documents 212 checks (tools/smoke_test.js), 80 checks (tools/impact_test.js), 71 checks (tools/integration_test.js), 25 and 24 checks (tools/poll_fixture_test.js, two different transports), 47 checks (tools/verify_reporters_test.js), 26 regression groups (tools/regression_test.js) and 26 Python tests. The old figures survive nowhere in the repository. Two new facts were also added to the entry because they change what the site can honestly claim: all 30 official club channels answered HTTP 403 to the CI runner on 2026-09-18, and 10 of 30 teams have a Bluesky-verified in-arena writer whose feed is polled automatically while 13 have no writer account at all.

irregularities.title: NFLInjuryReport documents a missed-alert incident, not just an abstract latency caveat
irregularities.detail: The repository's README section 4 records that on 2026-09-17 two in-game injuries produced no alert, and that the post-mortem measured a median gap of 188 minutes between published snapshots over the eight days to 2026-09-18 against a nominal 10-minute schedule. The source ledger (re-probed 2026-09-18) shows the ESPN scoreboard endpoint answering HTTP 200 keylessly and being used to decide which clubs are in a game window. This is recorded here because 'refreshed every 10 minutes' is a schedule, not a latency guarantee, and readers of this directory should not treat any of these feeds as time-critical. The entry now says so.

irregularities.title: TradingViewTheLeap's README pointed at an older capture file than the one in its repository
irregularities.detail: The README names research/evidence/TV-CONTEST-AMP-SEP2026-2026-09-18-R8.md as the latest official contest capture, but GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/TradingViewTheLeap/contents/research/evidence also returns TV-CONTEST-AMP-SEP2026-2026-09-18-R9.md, a later same-day capture (accessed approximately 17:00 UTC) that recorded 96,707 participants and the top 250 rows. The description was therefore sourced from the evidence file, not the README line, and says which. The repository's own pass history also reads twelfth-pass audit (PASS12) alongside an 'eleventh pass' section, so its internal pass numbering should not be treated as a reliable version counter.

irregularities.title: Stale narrative, not missing repositories, is the dominant error mode
irregularities.detail: This audit re-read every API-derived field for all 39 entries and found drift in ten, but only one was structurally wrong (WoWForever, a site the previous audit could not see). The rest were descriptions that had quietly stopped being true: one false classification (StockPaperSim), one set of entirely superseded counters (KalshiPaperSim), one set of stale test counts (NBAInjuryReport), one omitted incident (NFLInjuryReport) and one lagging evidence pointer (TradingViewTheLeap). The generator keeps the numbers honest; nothing currently forces the prose to be re-read, so every future refresh should assume the prose is the stale part and check it against the repository rather than against the previous audit.

irregularities.title: A repository was created in the middle of the audit and had to be listed from its file listing alone
irregularities.detail: GET /users/buffedlizard55-lab/repos returned 40 public repositories when the audit started and 41 by the end: Elections was created at 2026-09-18T22:42:36Z, roughly two minutes after data/sites.js was generated, and its first and only commit is 18e1243 'Initial commit' at 22:42:37Z. It is listed in this directory because it satisfies every inclusion rule and the brief asks for all Pages sites, but its description is deliberately nothing more than its own file listing - a single 11-byte README.md reading '# Elections' - because no content exists to source a real description from, and inventing one would break the one rule this project keeps. Anyone reading this entry should treat it as a placeholder whose purpose is unknown to the audit. Expect it to look completely different at the next refresh.

irregularities.title: Elections was published with a description that had become false — the same error class as IRR-25
irregularities.detail: The 2026-09-18 audit listed Elections as 'Single-commit placeholder repository ... one README.md of 11 bytes', which was true when written (IRR-31). By the 2026-09-20 audit the repository had 46 commits, a 18,646-byte README, an index.html plus src/ site, docs/, data/, backtest/, contest/ and test/ directories — a verification-first election intelligence project that backtests polls and prediction markets against verified official outcomes. The entry was rewritten from the repository's own README, its classification changed from stub to app, and its category moved out of Directory & Meta. Twice in three audits a placeholder grew into a full site between snapshots; descriptions of young repositories should be treated as the most perishable text in this directory.

irregularities.title: KalshiPaperSim's AUTO:COUNTS block moved on every quoted figure for the second audit in a row
irregularities.detail: Read from the repository's own machine-regenerated AUTO:COUNTS block (scripts/render-docs.js): 2026-09-18 -> 2026-09-20: 99 -> 101 verified facts (34 -> 36 documented), 45 -> 50 flagged irregularities, 41 -> 43 strategies, 10,905 -> 12,754 captured daily candlesticks across 53 -> 114 replayable markets, 112 -> 125 automated tests, 13 -> 15 Live Desk entrants on 62 -> 80 real open contracts. Nine real markets is the only quoted value that has never moved. The entry quotes the block with its read date, per the IRR-26 rule.

irregularities.title: NBAInjuryReport's published test counts could not be found anywhere in its README and were deleted, not restated
irregularities.detail: The 2026-09-18 entry stated a 212-check smoke test, 80-check impact test, 71-check integration test, 25-check and 24-check poller fixtures and a 47-check reporter verifier. In the 2026-09-20 README those exact figures appear nowhere — the run/test block now names tools without counts and adds tools/intelligence_test.js (reporter-ledger forward scoring). The reporter-coverage flag also flipped: re-measured 2026-09-19, 18 of 30 teams have a Bluesky-verified in-arena writer (was 10), the other 12 a bio-verified pollable writer (was 7), and 0 have no writer account (was 13) — the direction of the change shows how fast the human layer moved.

irregularities.detail: Read from the repository (2026-09-20): the 2026-09-19 sessions (v19-v21) added 8,369 new verified entries, expanded the ClinicalTrials.gov Phase 3 registry from 4,212 to 10,664 studies across 2024-2029 and the verified stock-snapshot store from 979 to 2,848 rows, and extended the pre-1980 decision table back to 1965 (125 new rows, 173 total over 15 years) with a full-database cross-check of 477 = 477 classifiable ORIG/AP rows.
