irregularities.title: A second repository was created minutes before the audit read it and had to be listed from its file listing alone
irregularities.detail: VacationSchedule was created 2026-09-20T00:48:59Z, roughly ten minutes before this audit generated its dataset at 00:58:56Z. Its only commit is daa0fcd 'Initial commit' (2026-09-20T00:49:00Z) and its entire contents are an 18-byte README.md reading '# VacationSchedule'. Pages reports 'built' from main /. Like Elections in IRR-31, it satisfies every inclusion rule but has no content to source a real description from, so its entry states only its own file listing; its purpose is unknown to the audit and its category is a neutral holding bucket. SUPERSEDED WITHIN THE HOUR: the content commit 4712716 landed at 2026-09-20T01:31:55Z, fourteen minutes after that snapshot was generated, and turned the placeholder into the Free Time Scoreboard project described in IRR-42. This entry is kept as the record of what the audit could honestly see at the time, not as a current description of the repository.

irregularities.title: VacationSchedule was published as an 18-byte placeholder and is now a full project — the third consecutive audit in which this has happened
irregularities.detail: The 2026-09-20T01:17:26Z audit listed VacationSchedule truthfully as 'Single-commit placeholder repository ... one README.md of 18 bytes ... no index.html, no application code and no research content' (IRR-41). Fourteen minutes later commit 4712716 (merged as 83663f7 at 2026-09-20T01:32:24Z) added a complete project: a 6,554-byte README, site/index.html, a 26,658-byte site/app.js, a 96 KB generated data bundle, scripts/, docs/ (5 files), tests/ (39 tests) and data/verified/ + data/analysis/. Re-verified 2026-09-20 via GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/VacationSchedule (3 commits, 91 KB), GET .../git/trees/main and GET .../contents/README.md. The published description was therefore flatly false for about an hour, and would have stayed false until the next refresh. This is the same error class as IRR-25 (StockPaperSim) and IRR-33 (Elections) — a description that was true when written and false by the next read — and it has now occurred in three consecutive audits, every time in a repository less than 48 hours old. The entry was rewritten from the repository's own files, its title and category replaced, and the 'Personal & Placeholders' category retired because it no longer holds anything.

irregularities.title: VacationSchedule's built app is not what its GitHub Pages URL serves
irregularities.detail: GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/VacationSchedule/pages reports status 'built' from source `main /`, but the application lives in the `site/` subdirectory and GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/VacationSchedule/contents/index.html?ref=main returns HTTP 404 — there is no index.html at the published path. https://buffedlizard55-lab.github.io/VacationSchedule/ therefore renders only Jekyll's markdown view of README.md, while the scoreboard app the repository actually built (site/index.html + site/app.js + a 96 KB data bundle) is unreachable from it. The repository's own README gives local-run instructions (`cd site && python3 -m http.server 8080`) instead of a live link, which is consistent with the app never having been published. This directory classifies the entry 'stub' because `kind` means 'what the published URL serves', not 'does the repository contain app code' — both facts are stated on the entry so neither is lost. Owner fix: either move the site payload to the repository root, or set Settings -> Pages to publish `main /site`. Same class as the StockPaperSim root-redirect note and ShoulderPain's 403 on Pages settings.

irregularities.title: Elections reports three different totals for its own irregularity register
irregularities.detail: Re-verified 2026-09-20 at commit facd343 by reading the repository's own files. (a) README.md states '49 flagged irregularities/discrepancies ... (Node items 1-12 + 23-49; Python-track items 13-22)' in two separate places. (b) IRREGULARITIES.md contains 58 numbered table rows, 1 through 58 with no gaps. (c) data/irregularities.json contains 48 items whose ids are exactly 1-12 and 23-58, so with the Python-track 13-22 held in data/flagged_sources.json the real register total is 58. (d) IRREGULARITIES.md's own header adds a fourth figure, claiming its JSON twin covers 'Node-track items 1-12 + 23-53' — five items short of the 58 the JSON actually holds. The README also asserts that its lint fails if the table and the JSON drift apart, and that check is not catching this. This directory quotes 58, the number of rows actually present, and flags the discrepancy on the entry rather than repeating the README's 49. Reproduce: GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/Elections/contents/IRREGULARITIES.md and .../data/irregularities.json.

irregularities.title: Elections' README contradicts itself on its Node test count, and the figure moved 70 -> 82 in two days

Two days ago the same two rows read 70 and 45. Reproduce: GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/Elections/contents/README.md and compare the 'Checks' table row with the `test/` row of the 'What's here' table.

irregularities.title: OLBG-Competition's automated test count moved 105 -> 126 between two audits on the same day
irregularities.detail: The 2026-09-20T01:17:26Z audit read 105 offline pytest tests from the repository's README. Commit 027cf93 'Add licensed odds and verified result adapter contracts' (merged as a371b63 at 2026-09-20T02:03:13Z) took it to 126, stated identically in the README's 'What is built' list and its repository-layout block, and added a permissioned The Odds API historical-odds connector plus an authorization-gated official-organizer result adapter (both inactive). Re-verified via GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/OLBG-Competition/commits?sha=main and .../contents/README.md.

irregularities.title: ShoulderPain changed state three times inside a single audit, once 60 seconds after this directory had stamped it verified
irregularities.detail: The clearest instance yet of the staleness class this repository exists to catch, and the first observed happening repeatedly *inside* one audit run. irregularities.title: The overlay stamped only a timestamp, so a repo that moved after its prose was read was undetectable — fixed with a recorded commit SHA, which then caught five moves in one pass
irregularities.detail: Design defect found and fixed during this audit. README task #3 asked for a per-entry `lastVerified` date so a reader could tell which descriptions were re-read this cycle. That was implemented, and IRR-47 immediately proved it inadequate: ShoulderPain's default branch moved at 2026-09-20T02:42:19Z, 60 seconds after its stamp of 02:41:19Z was written, so the stamp said 're-read in the latest pass' about a repository state that no longer existed. A date answers 'when did someone look', not 'is what they wrote still what is there'. Every entry therefore now also carries `verifiedAtSha` — the 7-character default-branch commit its prose was read against — and tools/build_data.py compares it with the live `lastCommitSha` at build time, emitting `proseStale` per entry and `counts.proseStale` in aggregate. The comparison is exact and free: no re-reading required, and a future session can list every entry whose prose is provably behind its repository before deciding what to read. Entries whose prose was carried forward record the prior audit's SHA rather than being left blank, so a carried entry is stale only if its repository actually moved. MasterSite's own entry is the one deliberate exception: its description describes this directory rather than a fetched README, so it is stamped with the SHA current when the description was last written and will always read stale immediately after a push. Limitation that remains: a matching SHA proves the prose was read against those bytes, not that it is still *true* — a repository can be accurate at one commit and wrong at the next without either changing (IRR-04 to IRR-06). What each build actually reported, in order: the first build after `verifiedAtSha` was added flagged 3 entries behind their repositories — GEMSDOE (session 19 had landed, superseding the session-18 status the description quoted), SFWeather (session 14) and ShoulderPain (a fourth commit) — all three of which had been re-read and stamped earlier in the *same* session, so a timestamp stamp would have called them current. After those were re-read, the next build flagged exactly 1: DrugAnalysis, whose prose had been *carried* from the prior audit at 6cb77f6 and whose v21.1 pre-1980 spine landed mid-build at b6cdb8a. Re-reading it, the next build flagged 2 more — SFWeather again (36fa2e4 to 42f9892, an automated data-only refresh that left README.md untouched, so its prose was re-verified by line-by-line diff and re-stamped rather than rewritten) and VacationSchedule (83663f7 to 6488222, which changed every window it recommends; IRR-52). The build after that flagged a fifth, OLBG-Competition (a371b63 to fee61ea), which had added an entire ice hockey pipeline and moved its test count 126 to 144 (IRR-54). Across the second pass the gate fired seven times on six distinct repositories, every one caught mechanically. Note which entries the detector caught: GEMSDOE, SFWeather and ShoulderPain had been re-read minutes earlier in the same session, but DrugAnalysis and OLBG-Competition were *carried* forward from earlier passes — precisely the entries a human auditor would least think to re-check, and the ones whose prose had actually gone false. The rebuild that reports `0 provably behind their repo` is the pass's completion gate: it means all 44 descriptions were read at the commit the repository is still at, which no timestamp can assert. Reproduce: run `python3 tools/build_data.py` and read the `PROSE-STALE` lines; the check is `entry.verifiedAtSha == repo head SHA`, using the same `gitHead` value the live dataset already records for every entry.

irregularities.title: GitHub Pages `status` is a live state machine, so a snapshot can record a healthy site as 'building' — the generator now waits and re-reads
irregularities.detail: Observed directly during this audit. The build that ran at 2026-09-20T02:57Z recorded `pagesBuilt: 43` of 44, the one exception being SFWeather with `pagesStatus: 'building'`. A re-read of GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/{repo}/pages for all 44 entries 12 seconds later returned `built` for every one, including SFWeather. The cause is not a defect in the repository or the directory: SFWeather's own automated nightly commit 42f9892 'data: refresh NOAA/NWS/NCEI/CPC sources [skip ci]' had landed at 02:57:39Z, seconds before the read, and GitHub Pages was mid-deploy. `status` is therefore a transient property of the deployment at the instant of the read, not a durable property of the repository — the same class of asynchrony as `size` (IRR-04 to IRR-06), but with a worse failure mode, because publishing '43 of 44 built' reads as 'one site is broken' when the truth is 'one site was rebuilding'. Fix applied to tools/build_data.py: when a Pages read returns any status other than 'built', the generator now re-reads that endpoint up to four times at six-second intervals before recording it, prints how many re-reads it needed, and still records a genuinely non-built status as-is with a warning if it persists — so a real broken build is never masked, only a transient one. Any future audit whose dataset reports fewer built sites than listed entries should re-read the endpoint before treating it as a finding.

irregularities.title: GitHub credentials expired mid-audit at ~2026-09-20T03:07Z, blocking the live re-verification, the push and the pull request for about two hours (resolved 04:54Z)
irregularities.detail: Recorded because it bounds what this audit can claim, and because the failure is silent in a dangerous way. The dataset published here was generated successfully at 2026-09-20T03:06:19Z (44 entries, 2,360 commits, all 44 Pages builds reporting `built`, 0 entries behind their repository head). Roughly one minute later every GitHub read began failing: `gh auth status` reports 'The github.com token in GH_TOKEN is no longer valid', `gh api repos/buffedlizard55-lab/MasterSite` returns HTTP 401 'Bad credentials', and — the part that makes this easy to miss — a plain unauthenticated `curl https://api.github.com/users/buffedlizard55-lab` also returns 401 rather than the usual 200, so the sandbox's egress credential itself is what expired, not a per-request token. Three consequences, stated plainly rather than papered over. (1) tools/verify_live.py was run after the expiry and returned 51 checks with every one a 'MISMATCH ... committed=200 live=401'; that output is an artifact of the auth failure and NOT a finding about the data, so tools/last_live_verify.json was restored from git to the last valid run (2026-09-20T01:17:26Z, 582 checks, 0 hard mismatches). A future session must not read the 401 run as 44 broken entries. (2) tools/audit_descriptions.py could not be re-run at all because it fetches each repository's README to diff against the published description; tools/last_description_audit.json is therefore a labelled PARTIAL artifact whose `unresolved` list predates the final edits to ShoulderPain and Elections. (3) `git push` failed with 'could not read Username for https://github.com', so at that moment the branch existed only as a local commit on arena/01a0bc90-mastersite, with no pull request opened and nothing merged. Two mitigations were verified while access still worked, so the published content itself is sound: the generator's own prose-staleness gate reported `0 provably behind their repo` for all 44 entries at the 03:06:19Z build, and no published artifact reads either verifier output file (tools/build_data.py, tools/build_verification.py, index.html and app.js were each grepped). Reproduce the failure: `gh auth status`, then `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://api.github.com/users/buffedlizard55-lab`. Resolution needs the account owner to reconnect GitHub; on reconnect the required sequence is re-run verify_live.py, re-run audit_descriptions.py, then push and open the pull request. Because these repositories commit continuously (IRR-42, IRR-50, IRR-52, IRR-54), the reconnect must also re-run build_data.py first — the 03:06:19Z snapshot will very likely already be behind by then. RESOLVED 2026-09-20: the owner reconnected GitHub at approximately 04:54Z. The prescribed sequence was then followed exactly rather than pushing the stale snapshot — a full build_data.py rebuild first, which reported 4 entries behind and grew total commits from 2,360 to 2,398, then re-read and rewrite, then rebuild again, repeating until the gate reported 0 provably behind (four builds, ten further moves, IRR-61), then build_verification.py, then all three verifiers, all of which ran clean: verify_live.py 582 of 582 checks with 0 hard mismatches and 0 drift, audit_descriptions.py 0 entries needing manual confirmation against 7 documented exceptions, and audit_kind.py 44 of 44 re-derived with 0 disagreements. The bogus 401 run and the PARTIAL description-audit artifact were both replaced by real runs. Final snapshot 2026-09-20T05:15:50Z, 2,413 commits, 62 irregularities.

Both were found by counting and grepping rather than by reading the summary. The description above quotes the banner for capture completeness and verdicts and the body for the sixteenth-pass figures, and says which is which. Note that the banner's own caveat is the important part and is unchanged in substance: captures are Yahoo vendor-tier and not exchange-verified, the Alpaca IEX route (`make official-bars`) is still blocked on environment credentials, and no authenticated TradingView Strategy Report export is available.

irregularities.title: KalshiPaperSim maintains a ledger that audits THIS directory; one of its findings against us is now itself stale, and one of its sources 404s
irregularities.detail: Found while re-reading KalshiPaperSim at f37eeaa. Its README carries a section titled 'Signal sources (the MasterSite review)' which states that the owner's master directory of verified GitHub Pages sites — linking https://buffedlizard55-lab.github.io/MasterSite/, i.e. this project — 'was reviewed site by site (2026-09-18) against one question: could this project supply a verified, point-in-time signal that a Kalshi strategy here could trade on?', with the full ledger in src/signal-sources.js rendered in its Research tab. So a sibling repository is consuming this directory as an input and recording verdicts on its entries, which makes this directory's accuracy someone else's dependency. Three of its claims were checked against the official GitHub REST API on 2026-09-20. (1) COVERAGE: it names three repositories this directory could plausibly have missed — PriceKalshiHistorical, PFFNFL and NFLPRED. All three return HTTP 200 on both GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/{name} and /pages, and all three are listed here, so there is no coverage gap; the build's own assertion that listed + unlisted equals the account's 45 Pages sites independently confirms it. (2) CORROBORATION: it reports 'NFLPRED is an empty stub (one README, verified)'. This directory classifies NFLPRED as kind=stub with 1 commit and size 0, and listing its root returns a single 9-byte README.md — two independent audits agree. It also reports that no CEO repository exists among the account's public repos (its irregularity #32), and GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/CEO returns HTTP 404, consistent with this directory listing no such entry. (3) A FINDING AGAINST US THAT HAS SINCE BEEN FIXED: its irregularity #42 states that this directory's record for StockPaperSim 'is stale'. That was true when written on 2026-09-18 and was corrected in the 2026-09-20 audit (IRR-37, Season 2 roster 14 to 19); StockPaperSim was re-read and re-stamped at 12fd8f2 during this audit, so the state KalshiPaperSim objected to no longer existed — and within nine minutes of that check the repository moved again to 560efa8, landing a SEC Form 4 insider lane (IRR-61), so its #42 flag is now two states out of date. That sequence is worth stating precisely, because it cuts both ways: their finding was correct when written, our correction was correct when made, and neither stays correct for long. This entry's verifiedAtSha is 560efa8. (4) ONE OF ITS SOURCES 404s: its PinePilot row describes a Pine Script lab whose 'TA families are already the roster's trend/momentum/mean-reversion entries', but GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/PinePilot returns HTTP 404 and GET /pages likewise, so the repository it cites as a testable archetype is not reachable — the same failure mode as JobSearchSF (IRR-01), in a repository that is not ours to fix. Recorded here because a reader following that ledger will hit a dead link, and because it is a useful reminder that a verified claim can be true when written and unreachable later.

irregularities.title: Four more repositories moved in the nine minutes between re-reading them and rebuilding, including one that falsified a claim this audit had just written
irregularities.detail: The clearest demonstration yet that the prose-staleness gate has to run last, not first. GitHub credentials were restored at about 2026-09-20T04:54Z and the snapshot was rebuilt at 04:55Z, reporting 4 entries behind (Commodities, KalshiPaperSim, ShoulderPain, TradingViewTheLeap). All four were re-read against their repositories' own files and rewritten between 04:57Z and 05:04Z. The rebuild at 05:05Z then reported 4 DIFFERENT entries behind — OLBG-Competition (fee61ea to 8b0bd8c), SFWeather (42f9892 to d4a7787), ShoulderPain again (8a21b94 to 06eec87, nine minutes after it had been rewritten) and StockPaperSim (12fd8f2 to 560efa8) — and total commits had moved 2,398 to 2,411. ShoulderPain is now on its fifth verified state inside one audit and StockPaperSim's move is the sharpest case: IRR-60 had been written minutes earlier asserting that StockPaperSim's stamp 12fd8f2 equalled its current head SHA, which was true when checked and false by the next build, so IRR-60 itself had to be corrected — an irregularity entry invalidated by the churn it was describing. Each of the four was then triaged by fetching both README revisions and diffing, rather than assumed: StockPaperSim was material (a new SEC Form 4 agent lane with 65 filings and 99 parsed transactions across ten tickers, tests 634 to 648, audit checks 1,870 to 1,871, LIMITATIONS.json 43 to 44) and was rewritten; ShoulderPain changed by one README line (a session branch name) but its REVIEW.md ledger count moved 89 to 90, confirmed by re-fetching data/claims.json as a 90-item array, so one number in the description was corrected and the rest re-counted; SFWeather gained session 15 in 8 changed README lines, all test inventories, and every figure the description quotes was grep-confirmed present at identical frequency in both revisions; OLBG-Competition's README was not touched at all (README_changed=false, 7 files, a max-drawdown arithmetic fix in code and a licence re-verification), so it was re-stamped rather than rewritten. Tallying the whole 2026-09-20 audit: the gate fired 17 times across 7 builds on 10 distinct repositories — GEMSDOE (twice), SFWeather (four times, five successive heads), ShoulderPain (three times), DrugAnalysis, VacationSchedule, OLBG-Competition (twice), Commodities, KalshiPaperSim, TradingViewTheLeap and StockPaperSim — and only the eighth build reported 0 (IRR-42, IRR-49, IRR-50, IRR-52, IRR-54, IRR-56 to IRR-58, IRR-61, IRR-62). Operational consequence recorded for future sessions: re-reading and rebuilding must be treated as one loop that repeats until the gate reports 0, not as two steps, and any claim of the form 'repository X is unchanged' has a shelf life of minutes. Reproduce: run `python3 tools/build_data.py` twice about ten minutes apart and compare the PROSE-STALE lines.

irregularities.title: This directory's own GEMSDOE description quoted one replicate of a twice-fired measurement, which its source explicitly forbids — caught only because an evidence-only commit was read instead of waved through
irregularities.detail: A defect in this directory's prose, not in the repository's, and the most instructive catch of the audit because the mechanism that found it was not the one designed to. The prose-staleness gate reported GEMSDOE behind at 3093c6b; the intervening commit 0ca1466 is 'evidence(pseudo-labels): fold 0 with SGMC pseudo, paired vs no-pseudo baseline [skip ci]', touching 6 files at +1/-1 each and changing neither README.md nor STATUS.md. By the shortcut reasoning recorded for SFWeather in IRR-61 — automated commit, prose files untouched, therefore re-stamp — this would have been waved through. Instead the six files were fetched, because they are evidence rather than data refreshes, and data/evidence/pseudo_labels/fold0_two_population_contrast.json now reports verdict GAIN_ON_THE_COMBINED_SURROGATE with proxy +0.067719 and catalogue -0.107890. Those are not the +0.1036 (P=0.999) / -0.0874 (P=0.001) / TRADE_OFF_PROXY_GAINS_CATALOGUE_LOSSES values the published description quoted. Reading STATUS.md — byte-identical at both commits, so the gate could not have flagged it — explains why: the measurement has fired twice, and STATUS.md states that 'The effect is the size of the replicate noise. The first fire measured proxy +0.1036 (P = 0.999) and catalogue -0.0874 (P = 0.001); this fire, same seed, same config, same partition, different runner, measured proxy +0.0677 and catalogue -0.1079', a ~0.036 run-to-run swing on the proxy arm of the same order as the +0.0313 union contrast itself. It adds that the two scopes disagree in sign on the union (+0.0313 held-out vs -0.0375 trained-on), which is 'instability, not a result', that read against the bar the repository's own FIELD rule uses (paired block bootstrap P >= 0.95) the union contrast reaches only P = 0.916 with an interval spanning zero on 8 scoreable blocks, making it 'suggestive, not established', and — the operative sentence — 'Eight blocks is not a sample. Both fires' numbers are in git history; the second overwrote the first's files, so quoting either one alone would overstate the precision.' The description did precisely that: it quoted the first fire alone and presented one derived verdict as the finding, so it was accurate about a number and misleading about the measurement. Corrected to carry both fires, the replicate swing, the scope sign disagreement, the P = 0.916 reading and the 0.197183-vs-0.1972 coincidence STATUS.md defuses on purpose. Two lessons recorded for future sessions. First, `verifiedAtSha` matching proves the prose was read against those bytes, not that it is true — the failing text had been read at 3093c6b minutes earlier and STATUS.md had not changed at all, so no SHA comparison could ever have flagged it; only reading the evidence the prose quotes did. Second, an evidence-only `[skip ci]` commit is not automatically benign: unlike a data refresh, evidence files are what a research description quotes, so they must be opened. Reproduce: GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/GEMSDOE/contents/data/evidence/pseudo_labels/fold0_two_population_contrast.json?ref=main and compare its `verdict` and `verdict_reason` with the pseudo-label table in STATUS.md item 2.

irregularities.title: MLBComp was published as a 'placeholder repository' while it had become a full 11-commit application — and the repository had meanwhile withdrawn its own fabricated data

irregularities.title: NFLComp's published PnL had changed sign: a claimed +$2,434,194.80 profit is in fact a -$353,618.85 loss, and every headline figure in the entry was stale

irregularities.title: Three repositories changed classification from 'stub' to 'app' in one day by adding a root index.html; the IRR-43 class of finding is now resolved for all of them

irregularities.title: Elections' README disagrees with Elections' own data files on three counts (209 vs 189 vs 229 sources; 63 vs 58 irregularities)
irregularities.detail: Elections' README headline says '209 sources' while its own source table in the same file says 'data/sources/master.json - 189 verified entries'. Loading that file gives 229 rows (status histogram: 221 verified, 3 verified-claim, 3 verified-via-search, 2 needs-review). Likewise the README says '63 flagged irregularities' while data/irregularities.json holds 58 items, with a highest id of 68 because the ids are non-contiguous — the same count-the-rows-don't-quote-the-number trap as IRR-51 (VacationSchedule) and the WoWForever claims ledger, whose own header comment warns against reporting the highest ID. The directory publishes the counted file values and deliberately does not publish the README's three figures. This is a finding about the upstream repository's internal consistency, not about its data quality; no source row was found to be wrong. Reproduce: python3 -c "import json;print(len(json.load(open('data/sources/master.json'))['sources']), len(json.load(open('data/irregularities.json'))['items']))" in a clone of Elections. RESOLVED IN PART AND RE-FORMED, re-measured at c41cc79 on 2026-09-23: the source-count divergence is closed — README.md's banner and source table both say 267 and json.load of data/sources/master.json returns 267, and the strings '209' and '189' no longer occur anywhere in that README (grep count 0 for both) — but two new divergences of the same class took its place. The README describes data/master_sources.json as '20 live-only entries' and data/flagged_sources.json as '7 excluded with reasons' where the files hold 6 and 4; and its banner's '84 irregularities' is the highest id in data/irregularities.json, whose item count is 74 with non-contiguous ids — the same id-versus-count confusion as the 63-versus-58 it replaced. The newest commit title adds a third number that matches nothing: 'Session 11: … 20 verified sources (249)'. This directory publishes the counted file values and names the README's as the README's. Reproduce: GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/Elections/contents/data/irregularities.json?ref=c41cc79 and compare its item count with the README banner.

irregularities.title: MLBRainDelay added: a new Pages site created mid-audit-cycle, verified by executing its own test suites rather than quoting them

irregularities.title: Twenty of fifty listed repositories had moved since the previous snapshot; four of the five most consequential findings came from commits that never touched a README
irregularities.detail: The 2026-09-21 pass opened with 20 of 50 entries reporting PROSE-STALE. Triaging them with GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/compare/{base}...{head} showed the pattern AGENTS.md predicts and then some: the README changed in only 13 of the 20 ranges, yet the README-unchanged ranges are where the sharpest findings were. GEMSDOE's range (25 files, no README) carried a whole Session 21 in STATUS.md that closed the project's standing data-placement blocker. NBAInjuryReport's range (3 files, no README) produced IRR-68. SFWeather's range (no README) added an entirely new published tier, a repair-and-maintenance executive summary with its own figures. TradingViewTheLeap's range (no README) still moved the audit banner past the description written two days earlier. Only WoWForever's single-commit, two-file range proved genuinely benign, and even there the 183-claim and 14-page counts were re-counted rather than assumed. The operational lesson to carry: a README-unchanged compare justifies triage, never a silent re-stamp. Reproduce: run python3 tools/build_data.py and read the PROSE-STALE block, then compare each range.

irregularities.title: Two empty repositories (SelfLearn, MasterSelfLearn) were created at 22:41Z while this audit was mid-run, taking the account to 53 public repositories

irregularities.title: MLBComp changed state twice during this single audit, from NO_SOURCE_SNAPSHOT to SOURCE_SNAPSHOT, forcing a second rewrite of a description written minutes earlier
irregularities.detail: MLBComp's entry was rewritten at 179c599 after IRR-64 found the published 'placeholder repository' description false. Two build passes later the generator reported it PROSE-STALE again: commit 41a7407 ('feat: source snapshot via api.github blobs, ingest 28k games, backtest 144k eval, research Q09-13, upcoming filter, PARTIALLY_VERIFIED registry, final report') had loaded a real source snapshot, moving data_mode from NO_SOURCE_SNAPSHOT to SOURCE_SNAPSHOT and total_simulated_bets from 0 to 144,098. irregularities.title: FUTURESCOMMODITIES expanded from 12 strategies to 17 one minute after its own tick ran, leaving the catalog and the committed competition state in disagreement

irregularities.title: Three of the ten new repositories publish from the branch root with no index.html there, so the Pages URL the READMEs link to serves a Jekyll-rendered README instead of the built site; two more solve the same problem with a forwarder page
irregularities.detail: GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/{repo}/pages returns status built, build_type legacy and source {branch main, path /} for all ten repositories added this pass. In legacy mode GitHub builds the branch root with Jekyll, so a repository with no root index.html publishes a rendered README rather than its built site. Three are in that state at the heads this pass read: LSTARENGY (built page at docs/index.html, 27,155 bytes), RGENGY (built site in site/, and .github/workflows/pages.yml uploads it with actions/upload-pages-artifact path: site then actions/deploy-pages — an Actions deployment path that a legacy build_type ignores) and StokEngineer (docs/index.html, 71,004 bytes, with README.md promising the site 'after Pages deploy'). All three are classified stub by the mechanical rule in tools/audit_kind.py — an index.html at the published path — even though each holds a real built site one directory down. Two repositories hit the same configuration and solved it with a forwarder, so they classify as app: SABERENGY's root index.html is a 146-byte meta-refresh to docs/ (commit f874c69 also corrected the README's Pages instructions to match the live config) and NFLPARLAYCOMP's is a 2,429-byte page that redirects to docs/ and explains the legacy build in its own body, added by commit b7e41a4 'Make the Pages site reachable; flag the Pages source misconfiguration'. irregularities.title: RESOLVED — Elections was the one repository of 62 whose GitHub Pages build was failing (status errored after two consecutive 'Page build failed.' builds); it recovered on its own push and now reports built
irregularities.detail: build_data.py re-reads a non-built Pages status up to four times at six-second intervals before recording it, precisely so that a repository pushed to seconds ago is not reported broken while it is still deploying (IRR-53). Elections survived that retry loop and is recorded as errored. GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/Elections/pages returns status errored with build_type legacy and source main /, and GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/Elections/pages/builds?per_page=3 shows the two most recent builds both errored with error.message 'Page build failed.' — build 1232488579 created 2026-09-22T18:02:45Z for commit b5b0334 ('Merge pull request #20 from buffedlizard55-lab/arena/01a0ca3c-election') and the build created 18:01:49Z for commit 968c95e — after a successful build at 17:59:55Z for commit f162127. The failure has therefore stood for more than five hours at the time of this snapshot, across two commits, and b5b0334 is still the repository's head. Elections does have a root index.html, so it is classified app; the errored status means the latest deployment did not succeed, and this directory records that as-is rather than inferring either that the URL is dead (GitHub continues serving the last successful build) or that it is healthy. It is the only non-built Pages status among the 62 public repositories on the account, so the snapshot's pagesBuilt reads 61 of 62 with one errored. The same repository is already the subject of IRR-67, where its README prose disagreed with its own regenerated data files. Reproduce: GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/Elections/pages/builds?per_page=3. RESOLVED by the repository's own push, re-read on 2026-09-23 at c41cc79: GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/Elections/pages now returns status built with source main /, and GET .../pages/builds?per_page=3 shows a successful build at c41cc79 above the two errored builds at b5b0334 and 968c95e that this entry recorded. The defect was real and was not the transient 'building' state IRR-53 describes — it persisted through four automatic re-reads over twenty minutes and two consecutive failed builds — but it is closed, and the 2026-09-22 snapshot's pagesBuilt 60 of 61 is superseded by 62 of 62 at the 2026-09-23 refresh and by 63 of 63 in the snapshot that ships, once NFL-PLAYER-PROP-SIM was listed and SelfLearn's transient 'building' state cleared. Recorded rather than deleted: this is the first Pages build failure this directory has caught and the first it has watched recover, which is the evidence that the four-read retry loop distinguishes a genuinely broken build from a deploy in progress in both directions.

irregularities.title: GitHub credentials expired mid-pass at ~2026-09-22T23:55Z, blocking the three API verifiers, the second data refresh and every further repository read; recorded as blocked, not passed
irregularities.detail: The same failure as IRR-55, and handled the same way. Evidence, all reproduced at 23:57Z: `gh auth status` reports 'X github.com: authentication failed — The github.com token in GH_TOKEN is no longer valid.'; GET https://api.github.com/repos/buffedlizard55-lab/Commodities returns HTTP 401 with body {"message": "Bad credentials"} — and returns the identical 401 when the request carries NO Authorization header at all, which shows the sandbox egress path is injecting the expired token into every api.github.com call, so falling back to the unauthenticated 60-request tier is not available either; GET https://api.github.com/rate_limit returns the same 401 with no X-RateLimit headers; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/buffedlizard55-lab/Commodities/main/README.md returns HTTP 000 (SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL, the documented egress restriction that also blocks *.github.io); `git clone https://github.com/buffedlizard55-lab/Commodities.git` fails with 'could not read Username for "https://github.com": terminal prompts disabled' and still fails with an empty credential.helper, so repository contents can no longer be read at a chosen commit either. Only github.com HTML answers (HTTP 200). WHAT WAS COMPLETED BEFORE THE EXPIRY, and is therefore live-verified rather than carried: a full `python3 tools/build_data.py` refresh ran to completion at 2026-09-22T23:32:49Z with working credentials and rewrote every API-derived field of all 61 listed entries, discovered the tenth new repository (PRICINGEXPERT) and reported the 23-entry prose-staleness queue; all ten new repositories were cloned and counted from their own files, with four test suites executed (FLABSENGY 79 passed, NFLPARLAYCOMP 103 OK with 1 skipped, ParlaySports 60 OK, RGENGY 460 OK) plus Coupons 53, SelfLearn 156 and MasterSelfLearn 350 before the expiry. WHAT IS BLOCKED AND IS NOT CLAIMED AS PASSED: tools/verify_live.py, tools/audit_kind.py and tools/audit_descriptions.py were not run at all, because a run under uniform 401 reports every entry as a mismatch and IRR-55 records that such a run must be discarded rather than committed; tools/last_live_verify.json and tools/last_description_audit.json are left at their committed 2026-09-21 values; the triage of the 21 remaining PROSE-STALE entries could not be performed because it needs a compare endpoint and a README read per entry; and no second refresh could pick up PRICINGEXPERT. The narrative work completed after the expiry was landed with `python3 tools/build_data.py --overlay-only`, which makes no network call and leaves `generated` and every API-derived field byte-identical, so the published snapshot states openly that its API half is from 23:32:49Z and its narrative half was re-rendered later. Per AGENTS.md a full build_data.py run plus all three verifiers is still required before this is published; this entry is the record that it did not happen, not a claim that it did. RESTORED, and the pass resumed: GitHub authentication was working again by 2026-09-23T00:44Z, when the full build_data.py refresh that this entry says was blocked ran to completion against the live API (62 listed sites, 3,526 commits, 62 of 62 Pages built, and an eleventh new repository discovered — NFL-PLAYER-PROP-SIM, IRR-88). The three verifiers were then run for real rather than left blocked, and their results are committed in tools/last_live_verify.json, tools/last_description_audit.json and this pass's build output. What the expiry did cost is not recoverable and stays on the record: the triage of the stale queue could not begin until the reconnect, so six repositories moved again in the interval and the queue the resumed pass inherited was 26 entries rather than 21, including four of this pass's own rewrites from an hour earlier (Coupons, FUTURESCOMMODITIES, LSTARENGY, SABERENGY, RGENGY and NFLPARLAYCOMP). The elapsed time between snapshot and publication is the real damage a credential expiry does, and it is measured in additional repository moves, not in lost findings.

irregularities.title: Landing this pass offline exposed three things --overlay-only could not do, one of which would have republished a classification the auditor had already proved false
irregularities.detail: Found while landing the post-expiry narrative work under IRR-85, and recorded so the next blocked session does not rediscover it. (1) KIND COULD NOT BE CORRECTED AT ALL. render_overlay_only()'s OVERLAY_FIELDS tuple listed title, category, description, flags, lastVerified, verifiedBasis and verifiedAtSha but not kind — yet main() sources kind from the overlay (`kind = ov.get("kind")`, falling back to an API index.html probe only when the overlay is silent), so for every entry that supplies it, kind is a curated field and not an API read. Three entries had provably changed classification this pass: NFLPARLAYCOMP gained a 2,429-byte root index.html forwarder in commit b7e41a4, and SelfLearn and MasterSelfLearn grew from one-commit placeholders into published sites with a root index.html (IRR-84). All three were stub in the snapshot and app in the overlay, and an overlay-only render would have republished 'stub' — a value this audit had already disproved from GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/index.html. "kind" is now in OVERLAY_FIELDS, with a comment saying why, and counts.apps / counts.stubs are recomputed beside the category tally for the same reason: they are derived from sites[] and build_verification.py quotes both into VERIFICATION.md, so rendering kind without them would publish a split that disagrees with the entries next to it. No API-derived field is touched by either change. (2) A CURATED REPOSITORY STILL CANNOT BE LISTED. PRICINGEXPERT was created at 2026-09-22T23:01:18Z, was seen and correctly withheld by the 23:32:49Z refresh ('no curated entry in tools/overlay.json — skipped from the directory'), and now has a complete overlay entry written from its own contents, but render_overlay_only iterates the sites already in the snapshot and can never add one. The consequence is visible in the published data: counts.unlisted still gives its reason as 'no curated entry in tools/overlay.json yet', which stopped being true the moment the entry was written. Both are corrected by the next full build, and neither was hand-edited, because counts.unlisted is generated. (3) THE GATE CAN REPORT AN ENTRY THAT IS AHEAD OF THE SNAPSHOT AS STALE. MasterSelfLearn commits its own output on a */30 cron, so it moved from fe488ed (the head the 23:32:49Z snapshot recorded) to eda549e while this pass was reading it, and the description was written against eda549e. proseStale is computed as verifiedAtSha != headSha, so the entry reports stale even though its prose was read at a NEWER commit than the snapshot knows about. That is the conservative output and it is left as-is: re-stamping the entry back to fe488ed to silence the gate would mean claiming the prose was read at a commit it was not read at. Only a full refresh resolves it.

irregularities.title: counts.proseReReadLatestPass measures 'shares the newest stamp', not 're-read this pass', so a pass that stamps as it goes publishes an undercount and the UI then calls brand-new entries 'carried'
irregularities.detail: Found while writing this pass's summary, and fixed in the data rather than in the counter. The field is computed as the number of entries whose lastVerified equals max(lastVerified) over all entries. That is only equal to 're-read in the latest pass' if a pass stamps everything it touches with one timestamp. This pass did not: it authored or re-read twelve entries at three instants as repositories moved under it (ten at 2026-09-22T23:20:00Z, NFLPARLAYCOMP at 23:45:00Z after IRR-82, SelfLearn and MasterSelfLearn at 23:50:00Z after IRR-84), so the counter reported 2 and the generator's own summary line printed 'prose: 2 re-read this pass, 59 carried'. The consequence is not only a wrong total. app.js derives the per-entry badge from the same comparison, so ten entries written for the first time in this pass — including nine repositories that did not exist 24 hours earlier — rendered as 'Prose carried', a state VERIFICATION.md section 4a defines as 'the prose is from an earlier pass'. The distortion was already known: app.js's legend carries the disclaimer 'This is not a count of all descriptions re-read during a multi-hour audit', and the previous pass recorded it in README.md rather than resolving it ('proseReReadLatestPass: 1 counts only entries sharing the single newest lastVerified timestamp, so it understates a multi-hour pass'). RESOLUTION: the counter's definition was left alone, because making it mean what its name says would require a pass boundary that neither overlay.json nor data/sites.js carries, and inventing one would be a new way to be wrong. Instead the twelve stamps were normalized to the pass stamp 2026-09-22T23:50:00Z — the newest of the three, so no entry's stamp moved backwards — and the published figures are now the honest ones: 11 of 61 listed entries re-read this pass (the twelfth, PRICINGEXPERT, is curated but cannot be listed without a full build, IRR-86), 50 carried, 21 provably behind. The per-entry read instants were not lost: each entry's verifiedBasis still names the commit it was read against and what was opened, which is where that detail belongs. Normalization does not weaken staleness detection, because proseStale compares verifiedAtSha with the recorded head SHA and never consults lastVerified. DURABLE RULE for the next session: stamp every entry a pass touches with one pass-completion timestamp, and put per-entry read times in verifiedBasis; a pass that stamps as it goes will under-report its own work and mislabel its newest entries as carried. Reproduce: python3 -c "import json;print(sorted({e['lastVerified'] for e in json.load(open('tools/overlay.json'))['entries'].values()}))" — before the fix this printed three 2026-09-22 stamps and the counter read 2; after it, one stamp and the counter reads 11. REFINED BY THE CASE IT DID NOT ANTICIPATE. The rule recorded above — stamp every entry a pass touches with one pass-completion timestamp — assumes a pass runs in one continuous window. This one did not: credentials expired at 23:55Z (IRR-85) and were restored after 00:44Z, so the pass has two stamp cohorts, 2026-09-22T23:50:00Z for the twelve entries read before the expiry and 2026-09-23T00:55:00Z for the six read after it. Normalizing all eighteen to the later stamp was considered and rejected, because six of the first cohort had gone PROSE-STALE in the interval — their repositories moved while the audit was blocked — so claiming they were verified at 00:55Z would assert a currency that the gate itself contradicts. The durable rule is therefore narrower than first written: stamp one timestamp per continuous working window, never per entry, and never bump a stamp forward for an entry the gate reports as behind. counts.proseReReadLatestPass consequently reports the newest cohort only (6), and the honest figure for the whole pass — 18 entries read or re-read, 12 before the expiry and 6 after — is stated here and in README.md rather than inferred from the counter.

irregularities.detail: Two findings in one range, and the second is the more serious. (1) The repository changed state three times in a single audit pass — 241d392, then 84f138f eight commits later (IRR-82), then fef877f four commits after that, 70 minutes after this directory had rewritten the entry from scratch. Across the last range the ledger shrank from 2,705 lines to 500 (-2,205), trades from 1,623 to 500, the state split from 541 EXECUTED / 1,082 SETTLED to 500 EXECUTED / 0 SETTLED, UNVERIFIED_DATA flags from 2,975 to 577, strategies from 37 to 52, and the docs/site_data/ bundles from 1,052 files and 7.62 MB to 1,057 files and 6.44 MB; the MISSING_DATA flag disappeared because the manifest it reported missing now exists with 6 rows; and a .nojekyll file was added at the root for the legacy Pages build. README.md did not change in the range, which is the IRR-70 case again: a README-unchanged compare carried every one of these findings. (2) The repository's own headline result now contradicts its own accounting. docs/site_data/leaderboard.json holds 1,000 users over which sum(total_pnl) = 0.00 and sum(win_rate) = 0.00 — every single user reads exactly zero — while sum(starting_bankroll) = 10,001,606.66 and sum(current_bankroll) = 9,919,682.37, a movement of -81,924.29, or -0.82 percent of the capital started. The internal explanation is visible in the same files and is not a bug in this directory's arithmetic: verification_report.json reports all 500 trades EXECUTED and none SETTLED, so no realized PnL has been booked anywhere, and the bankroll movement is capital committed, marks and fees rather than settled result. A reader who takes total_pnl for the competition's result reads 0.00; a reader who takes the bankrolls reads a loss of 81,924.29; an hour earlier the same files published -92,876.56 as the total. This directory publishes all three readings with their sources and resolves none of them, because choosing one would be an interpretation the repository does not license. This is the third headline-PnL defect this directory has caught (IRR-65 published a +$2.43M profit that was a -$353K loss; IRR-82 caught a sign flip before publication), and the first where the repository's own field and its own ledger disagree about whether anything has been settled at all. Reproduce: GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/NFLPARLAYCOMP/contents/docs/site_data/leaderboard.json?ref=fef877f and sum total_pnl, starting_bankroll and current_bankroll over its 1,000 users, then compare trades.by_status in data/competition/verification_report.json at the same ref.

irregularities.title: LSTARENGY was published as a four-file documentation stub and is now a 60-file research site whose own corrections section withdraws a price this directory published as fact — caught by audit_kind.py, not by the prose gate alone
irregularities.detail: The sixth stub-to-app reversal this directory has recorded (IRR-42, IRR-64, IRR-72, IRR-84 and now this), and the first where the repository corrected this directory's own prose. An hour after LSTARENGY was published as 'documentation-only ... The repository is four files: README.md plus docs/index.html, docs/styles.css and docs/.nojekyll', compare 0ac0b07...66d9c9b shows 3 commits and 60 files at +18,628/-7,768: a 217,302-byte root index.html, a root .nojekyll, src/ with 7 modules, tests/ with 5 node test files plus a browser spec, scripts/, web/, research/, two Actions workflows and a package.json. `npm run check` was executed in a clean clone and passed all three gates — '1..72 / # pass 72 / # fail 0' on Node v22.22.3, 'Traceability valid: 36 capabilities, 30 sources, 62 legacy review groups', and 'Verified 22 deterministic site assets. Both main:/ and main:/docs entrypoints are supported.' The register counts were then counted independently in docs/data/catalogue.json (sources 30, features 36, findings 10, inputs 9, sports 13, flags 14, roadmap 6) and docs/data/legacy-audit.json (entries 62), so they are measured twice rather than quoted once. DETECTION PATH: two independent verifiers flagged this entry, and only one of them would have caught it in the general case. The prose gate flagged it because README.md changed (+98/-33); tools/audit_kind.py flagged it because GET .../contents/index.html went from HTTP 404 to HTTP 200. Had the site been built without touching the README — exactly the IRR-70 case, and the reason this repository keeps a kind verifier separate from the description audit — the prose gate alone would have reported a README-unchanged range and invited a re-stamp over a classification that had just become false. THE SELF-CORRECTION: this directory published 'the published paywall pricing of 39.99 USD per month or 239.99 USD per year' as a single fact. The repository's own 'Important corrections to the old repository' section now records that the web pricing page displays $239.99/year while the US DraftKings app listing displays $269.99/year, that these are dated offers and not verified checkout totals or a universal price, and that 'Perfect Lineups is not established as paid-only' because the vendor guide advertises a free historical view. It also withdraws two of its own earlier claims — that standard algorithms are generally non-infringing (removed) and that 'self-healing' evidences reproducible nightly retraining (it does not) — and states that patent ownership, scope and enforceability were not independently established, which is why the four patent numbers this entry used to list bare are now published with that qualification. A directory that grades other projects' verification had a vendor price corrected by the repository it was grading. Reproduce: GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/LSTARENGY/compare/0ac0b07...66d9c9b, then git clone https://github.com/buffedlizard55-lab/LSTARENGY.git && npm run check.

irregularities.title: This pass publishes with 21 PROSE-STALE entries and 1 open description CHECK on the owner's explicit instruction to create and merge a PR — a recorded deviation from the completion gate, not a clean gate
irregularities.detail: AGENTS.md requires the full toolchain before publishing: a full tools/build_data.py run, verify_live.py, audit_descriptions.py and audit_kind.py, plus triage of the stale queue toward zero. The owner's instruction this session was 'create a PR and merge PR', and merging deploys through GitHub Pages. Rather than hold the work or declare the gate met, this pass publishes and states exactly where it stands. WHAT THE TOOLS SAID. tools/verify_live.py reported NO HARD MISMATCHES on the snapshot that ships, its only drift being repositories pushed after the snapshot read them; one build earlier it had reported a genuine hard mismatch on SelfLearn.pagesStatus committed='building' live='built' — the transient Pages state AGENTS.md warns about — and the prescribed fix, re-run build_data.py to fold it in, cleared it and took the account to built=63/63. tools/audit_kind.py: checked 63, derived 0, disagreements 0, after its single disagreement at the start of this turn (LSTARENGY overlay=stub vs live=app) was resolved by rewriting that entry from executed evidence (IRR-90). tools/audit_descriptions.py after `rm -rf tools/.readme-cache`: 27 accepted exceptions and 1 CHECK (TradingViewTheLeap, IRR-91). THE TREADMILL, which is why the queue is not at zero: tools/build_data.py was run in full eight times in this pass and reported account commit totals of 3,526 / 3,533 / 3,540 / 3,543 / 3,545 / 3,559 / 3,570 / 3,586 with stale-queue lengths of 21 / 21 / 21 / 21 / 22 / 24 / 26 / 27 — the last two readings taken after credentials were restored and the pass resumed — six readings taken within about two hours, each true when taken, and the entry you are reading was itself written after the sixth, so the snapshot that ships is a seventh reading whose counts appear in data/sites.js, VERIFICATION.md and the README table and are deliberately not restated here, because any number quoted in narrative would be falsified by the next build. In the sixth build MLB-Live-PBP was pushed at 01:20:19Z, about a minute after the snapshot had read it at 66 commits and 6d61092, and arrived at 68 commits and 859e958. WHAT WAS NOT DONE: the stale entries were not re-read to head. That queue cannot be drained to zero while 63 repositories are written to faster than they can be audited — eight builds in one pass, each finding new pushes, is the measurement — and the largest movers still open are NBAComp (58 commits ahead of its prose), KalshiPaperSim (48), Commodities (34) and OLBG-Competition (22). Each stale entry is badged in the UI with the SHA its prose was read at and the SHA the repository is now at, and the list is generated rather than hand-maintained. The Playwright contract in tests/directory.spec.js runs in CI and not locally, because no browser binary exists in this environment; this pass does not claim a local Playwright run. The deviation is recorded so that 'published' is never mistaken for 'gate clean'.

irregularities.detail: The 2026-09-23 pass completed every gate against the snapshot generated at 2026-09-23T01:37:24Z: tools/build_data.py (63 sites, 55 apps and 8 stubs, built 63/63, 3,561 commits, 64 public repositories, 64 Pages sites, counts.proseStale 24), tools/verify_live.py (829 checks, 828 ok, 0 hard mismatches, 1 drift), tools/audit_kind.py (63 checked, 0 derived, 0 disagreements) and tools/audit_descriptions.py (27 accepted exceptions, 1 CHECK). Neither could be executed — no push, no PR, no merge, and therefore no Pages deployment of this snapshot. This is recorded as blocked, not passed and not done. Nothing was published and nothing is claimed as merged. WHAT WAS DONE INSTEAD, following IRR-85's procedure: this IRR and its narrative were landed with `python3 tools/build_data.py --overlay-only`, which makes no network call, followed by `python3 tools/build_verification.py`; both read the existing snapshot, so every API-derived field in data/sites.js still reports the 01:37:24Z read rather than a guess. No verifier was re-run after 01:44Z and no run against uniform HTTP 401 was committed. THIS IS THE THIRD CREDENTIAL EXPIRY IN FOUR DAYS and the second in this session (IRR-55 ~2026-09-20T03:07Z, IRR-85 ~2026-09-22T23:55Z, this one ~2026-09-23T01:44Z), and the second time it has landed between finishing the work and publishing it. RESUME PROCEDURE: the owner reconnects GitHub in Arena; then re-run a full build_data.py plus all three verifiers, because the snapshot would be hours old and 64 repositories are being pushed to continuously, then push, open the PR against main and merge. RESOLVED AND EXECUTED at ~2026-09-23T02:24Z, when `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://api.github.com/rate_limit` returned 200 with no credentials offered and `gh auth status` reported the bot logged in again. The pass was pushed, a PR opened against main and merged, so this snapshot is published and the blockage lasted about 40 minutes. irregularities.title: Two entries in this directory's own dataset carried verifiedAtSha values that are not commit SHAs, making the staleness gate permanently unsatisfiable
irregularities.detail: build_data.py sets proseStale by comparing entries[*].verifiedAtSha with the live default-branch head SHA. Two curated entries held non-SHA strings: KalshiPaperSim held 'AUTO:COUNTS' and MasterSite held 'main'. Neither can ever equal a seven-character commit SHA, so both were reported PROSE-STALE by every build regardless of whether their prose had actually been read at head, and the UI badged them with 'read at AUTO:COUNTS' and 'read at main'. Two consequences: the gate silently became a permanent work item rather than a measurement, and the honest question the field exists to answer - was this prose read against these bytes? - had no answer for the two most-churned entries in the directory. The auto-generated-block label and the branch name had leaked into a field defined as a commit. Both are now resolved from executed evidence: KalshiPaperSim was re-read at 8a359bd with its suite run (157 tests, 157 pass) and MasterSite is stamped b1c9765 with the reason recorded in its verifiedBasis. A follow-up guard belongs in build_data.py: warn when an entry's verifiedAtSha is set but does not match ^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$, so a leaked label can never again masquerade as a stamp. Reproduce: inspect tools/overlay.json entries KalshiPaperSim and MasterSite in any commit before this pass, then compare with the printout 'PROSE-STALE KalshiPaperSim description read at AUTO:COUNTS' and 'PROSE-STALE MasterSite description read at main'.
